meta.what: the chip diagram's deep-zoom facts, fetched by the page (build_facts.py)

in.die.4.statement: Average density: 24 billion transistors over 570 mm2 is about 42 million per mm2, less than half the ~91 MTr/mm2 of TSMC N7's dense logic cells; SRAM periphery, analog blocks (PLLs, PHYs), I/O and wiring take the rest.
in.die.4.source: arithmetic on chip.process and chip.die-area; the N7 figure: Wikipedia, "7 nm process", comparison table, row TSMC N7 (gate pitch 57 nm, fin pitch 30 nm, minimum metal pitch 40 nm, 91.2-96.5 MTr/mm2, SRAM cell 0.027 um2; fins SAQP, gates and M0-M4 SADP), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_nm_process (read 30 Sep 2026)

size.die.statement: The ET-SoC-1 die: about 25.7 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 25.6-25.8 mm east-west by 22.1-22.2 mm north-south, scaled from Esperanto's die plot to 570 mm2 (chip.die-dims)
size.die.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.statement: Compute shire: about 3.72 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. one tile pitch: 3.73 mm east-west, 3.70 north-south, measured in pixels on the die plot (chip.hop-pitch)
size.shire.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.meshstop.statement: Mesh stop: about 500 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude only: nine 512-bit routers and their crossings; no floorplan of the shire is published (L114, l2.floorplan)
size.shire.meshstop.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.meshstop.router.statement: Router (one of nine main-NoC layers): about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: an 8-port router with 512-bit datapaths; the NetSpeed configuration is not in the repository
size.shire.meshstop.router.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.meshstop.router.buf.2.statement: If every slot holds one 512-bit flit, one router buffers 8 x 4 x 512 = 16,384 bits, about 147,000 bits over the nine layers of one stop.
in.shire.meshstop.router.buf.2.source: arithmetic on L105 with an estimated flit width (SYNTHESIS.md row "Flit width", unknown): inferred, the weakest of its inputs

size.shire.meshstop.router.buf.statement: Input buffers (virtual channels): about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 8 ports x 4 VC slots of a flit (512 bits or more) each, if flip-flops
size.shire.meshstop.router.buf.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.meshstop.router.alloc.statement: Route computation and allocators: about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: arbitration logic for 8 ports
size.shire.meshstop.router.alloc.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.meshstop.router.xbar.statement: Router switch (crossbar): about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: an 8 x 8 switch of 512-bit or wider datapaths
size.shire.meshstop.router.xbar.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.meshstop.xing.4.statement: The ET cell library has level shifters in both directions (vclevel_shft_h2l, vclevel_shft_l2h) and VCFIFO memories and synchronisers (vcfifo_mem, vcfifo_wr_hiv_*, vcfifo_wr_lov_*, et_cdc_sync) for these crossings.
in.shire.meshstop.xing.4.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.shire.meshstop.xing.statement: Voltage and clock crossing (VCFIFO): about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: a FIFO of a few 512-bit entries with level shifters on every bit
size.shire.meshstop.xing.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.cache.7.statement: At TSMC N7's 0.027 um2 high-density 6T cell, the shire cache's 40.3 Mbit of cells would take about 1.1 mm2, about 8% of the 13.9 mm2 shire tile, before the macros' periphery; which bitcell the macros use is not documented.
in.shire.cache.7.source: arithmetic on l2.bits and S.-Y. Wu et al. (TSMC), "A 7nm CMOS platform technology featuring 4th generation FinFET transistors with a 0.027um2 high density 6-T SRAM cell for mobile SoC applications", IEDM 2016, paper 2.6; the bitcell is asked (u.bitcell)

in.shire.cache.8.statement: "These SRAM banks operate near the process-nominal supply voltage to allow higher density than the smaller caches within each core."
in.shire.cache.8.source: D. Ditzel et al., "Accelerating ML Recommendation With Over 1,000 RISC-V/Tensor Processors on Esperanto's ET-SoC-1 Chip", IEEE Micro 42(3), May/June 2022 (https://www.esperanto.ai/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Dave-IEEE-Micro.pdf), p. 35

size.shire.cache.statement: Shire cache (four banks): about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 4 MB of SRAM macros (about 1.1 mm2 of bitcells if HD 6T, more with periphery) and their logic
size.shire.cache.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.bank.statement: Bank (one of four): about 700 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: a quarter of the shire cache
size.shire.bank.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.bank.reqq.statement: Request queue: about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 64 entries of address and state
size.shire.bank.reqq.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.bank.rbuf.statement: Read buffer: about 65 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 8 x 512 bits = 4,096 flip-flops at about 1 um2 each (an N7 flip-flop, inference) is about 0.004 mm2, 65 um on a side
size.shire.bank.rbuf.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.bank.dataq.statement: Data queue: about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 64 lines of 576 bits in a two-port register file
size.shire.bank.dataq.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.bank.atomic.statement: Atomic unit: about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: a 256-bit ALU
size.shire.bank.atomic.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.bank.pipe.statement: Bank pipeline: about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: the stage registers and control of one bank
size.shire.bank.pipe.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.subbank.statement: Sub-bank: about 350 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: four data panels of about 150 um plus a tag and a state macro
size.shire.subbank.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.subbank.tag.statement: Tag RAM (1,024 x 116 macro): about 70 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 118,784 bits at 0.027 um2 is 0.0032 mm2 (57 um square) of cells, more with periphery; if HD 6T (inference)
size.shire.subbank.tag.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.subbank.state.statement: Tag-state RAM (1,024 x 40, two-port): about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 40,960 bits; a two-port cell is larger than a 6T cell (order of magnitude)
size.shire.subbank.state.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.panel.statement: Data panel (4,096 x 144 SRAM macro): about 150 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 589,824 bits x 0.027 um2 = 0.016 mm2 of cells; if the array is 1,024 rows x 576 columns of 114 x 237 nm cells it is about 117 x 137 um, some 150 um with its periphery (inference on the unconfirmed m4 reading and the HD cell)
size.shire.panel.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.panel.array.4.statement: A 64-byte line read raises one wordline in each of 4 panels; 576 bits are sensed of the 2.36 million stored in the four panels.

size.shire.panel.array.statement: Bitcell array: about 137 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 1,024 rows x 114 nm = 117 um tall, 576 columns x 237 nm = 137 um wide, if HD 6T and 4:1 column mux (inference)
size.shire.panel.array.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.panel.decoder.statement: Row decoder and wordline drivers: about 120 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a strip the height of the array (inference)
size.shire.panel.decoder.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.panel.colio.statement: Precharge, column mux, sense amplifiers, write drivers: about 140 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a strip the width of the array (inference)
size.shire.panel.colio.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.panel.ctrl.statement: Clock gate and timing control: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.shire.panel.ctrl.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.subbank.ecc.statement: ECC (SECDED) logic: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: eight 72-bit XOR trees
size.shire.subbank.ecc.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.subbank.cmp.statement: Tag comparators: about 20 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: four 23-bit comparators
size.shire.subbank.cmp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.l2.statement: L2 (a partition of the shire cache): about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. spread over all 64 data panels: not a place of its own
size.shire.l2.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.l3.statement: L3 slice (a partition of the shire cache): about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. spread over all 64 data panels: not a place of its own
size.shire.l3.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.scp.statement: Scratchpad (a partition of the shire cache): about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. spread over all 64 data panels: not a place of its own
size.shire.scp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.uc.statement: UC block: about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: counters, interrupt logic and an atomic ALU
size.shire.uc.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.uc.flb.1.statement: The FLB extension provides 32 barrier counters, 8 bits wide, directly accessible by the threads in the shire, usable from user mode.
in.shire.uc.flb.1.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.327 (ch. 10)

in.shire.uc.flb.2.source: arithmetic on the PRM's 32 x 8-bit counters

size.shire.uc.flb.statement: Fast local barrier counters: about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 32 counters of 8 bits: a few hundred flip-flops
size.shire.uc.flb.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.uc.fcc.1.statement: Each hart has two credit-counter CSRs (four per minion); remote harts increment them through the CREDINC0-3 ESRs of the target shire; a read with no credit blocks until one arrives.
in.shire.uc.fcc.1.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.328 (ch. 11)

size.shire.uc.fcc.statement: Fast credit counters: about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 4 counters per minion
size.shire.uc.fcc.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.xbar.statement: Crossbar: about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. the specification routes the request crossbar "on top of all four banks": it spans the shire cache (l2.xbar.req)
size.shire.xbar.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.xbar.req.statement: Request crossbar: about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. as the crossbar
size.shire.xbar.req.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.xbar.rsp.statement: Response crossbar: about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. as the crossbar
size.shire.xbar.rsp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.neigh.4.statement: "Physical design plays an important role in chip architecture as 7-nm wires are relatively slow. We found it convenient to group eight ET-Minion cores together before wire length became a problem."
in.shire.neigh.4.source: D. Ditzel et al., "Accelerating ML Recommendation With Over 1,000 RISC-V/Tensor Processors on Esperanto's ET-SoC-1 Chip", IEEE Micro 42(3), May/June 2022 (https://www.esperanto.ai/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Dave-IEEE-Micro.pdf), p. 34

size.shire.neigh.statement: Neighbourhood: about 1.5 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. if 8 minions of about 0.25 mm2 plus the neighbourhood's logic make about 2.4 mm2, about 1.5 mm on a side (no floorplan published)
size.shire.neigh.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.neigh.icache.3.statement: The memory cells of the I-cache data RAMs need an HV region while the neighbourhood is LV, so the data RAMs were moved into the Shire Channel; an L1 I-cache hit takes around ten cycles.

in.shire.neigh.icache.4.statement: If each 512 x 144 macro holds 512 x 128 data bits (8 KB) plus ECC, the 32 KB cache is four macros, 16 per shire.
in.shire.neigh.icache.4.source: arithmetic on l1.icache-sram and neigh.composition; the 128 + 16 split is an assumption, so the result is inferred

size.shire.neigh.icache.statement: Instruction cache (32 KB): about 120 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. four 512 x 144 macros of 73,728 bits each; order of magnitude
size.shire.neigh.icache.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.neigh.l0.2.statement: The L0 microcache pipeline has five stages; each of the two (north and south) serves four minions over one shared bus.

size.shire.neigh.l0.statement: L0 micro instruction caches (two): about 80 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 2 x 16 x 512 bits = 16,384 bits of registers: about 0.01 mm2 (order of magnitude)
size.shire.neigh.l0.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.neigh.req.statement: Request path to the banks: about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.shire.neigh.req.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.neigh.rsp.statement: Response path from the banks: about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.shire.neigh.rsp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.neigh.pmu.statement: Performance counters (PMU): about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 12 counters
size.shire.neigh.pmu.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.shire.clock.2.statement: Five clocks in a minion shire: ref_clock (24/100 MHz pin), step_clk (400-1,000 MHz from PLL4 in the I/O shire), the shire's local DPLL output (1,000 MHz design), the DLL output for the four neighbourhoods (shire_clock shifted 180 degrees), and clk__noc (500 MHz design, from PLL2).
in.shire.clock.2.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.11-12 (§4.1, Table 2)

in.shire.clock.3.statement: Programmable clock delay lines: 25 ps steps (first specified at 100 ps), up to 1 ns, set by ESR, one per DLL feedback path.
in.shire.clock.3.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Shire DLL Delay Control.pdf, pdf p.4 (§2)

size.shire.clock.statement: Shire clock generation (PLL, DLL, delay lines): about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: a digital PLL and a DLL are each on the order of 0.01-0.05 mm2 (inference)
size.shire.clock.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.shire.sensors.statement: On-die sensors (temperature, process, voltage): about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: one small analog sensor block
size.shire.sensors.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.minion.3.statement: "The vector/tensor unit takes far more area than the integer pipeline"; "the entire ET-Minion, including its 4-KB L1 caches, operates on a single low-voltage power plane"; libraries were "recharacterized at 0.4 V".
in.minion.3.source: D. Ditzel et al., "Accelerating ML Recommendation With Over 1,000 RISC-V/Tensor Processors on Esperanto's ET-SoC-1 Chip", IEEE Micro 42(3), May/June 2022 (https://www.esperanto.ai/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Dave-IEEE-Micro.pdf), p. 33

size.minion.statement: Minion: about 500 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. if the 32 minions take one half to two thirds of the 13.9 mm2 tile, each is 0.22-0.29 mm2, about 0.5 mm on a side; no floorplan is published (l1.u-floorplan)
size.minion.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.minion.hart.3.statement: When two harts are enabled and ready, the thread scheduler alternates between them round robin; a hart that cannot issue (a hazard) is skipped.

size.minion.hart.statement: Hart (hardware thread): about 500 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a thread is not a place: its registers are spread through the core and the vector unit
size.minion.hart.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.core.2.statement: Five integer stages: ID (dependencies, register read), EX (ALU; an extra GSC stage for gathers and scatters), TAG (DCache tags), MEM (DCache data), WB.

size.core.statement: Integer pipeline (the core): about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. smaller than the vector unit (Esperanto: the vector/tensor unit takes far more area); order of magnitude
size.core.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.core.fe.1.statement: The front end (the document says 7 stages and describes stages 0-7): stage 0 sends the fetch, stages 1-5 wait a fixed time for the I-cache, stage 6 holds the double buffer and expands compressed instructions, stage 7 decodes and holds the thread scheduler. A taken branch requests its new PC in the TAG stage and kills the younger instructions; no branch predictor is described.

in.core.fe.2.statement: RTL modules: frontend_thread_buffer, frontend_thread_sched, frontend_rvc_expander, frontend_top.
in.core.fe.2.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.core.fe.statement: Front end (fetch, thread scheduler, decoder): about 80 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.core.fe.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.core.irf.1.statement: intpipe_rf instantiates rf_latch_2r_1w with WIDTH = 64 (XREG_SIZE) and ENTRIES = 2 threads x 32: a latch register file, 2 read ports and 1 write port.
in.core.irf.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.core.irf.2.statement: 64 x 64 = 4,096 storage latches per minion; at about 10 transistors each, some 41,000 transistors before the read multiplexers.
in.core.irf.2.source: arithmetic on intpipe_rf.v and the latch count of l1:g.latch-cell; the 10 transistors per latch are assumed, so the total is inferred

size.core.irf.statement: Integer register file: about 40 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 4,096 latch bits at roughly 0.15-0.2 um2 each (an HD latch, inference) is 0.0006-0.0008 mm2: about 25-30 um before the read trees, some 40 um with them
size.core.irf.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.core.alu.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.core.alu.2.statement: A fast 64-bit adder is a parallel-prefix adder (generate and propagate signals combined in about log2(64) = 6 levels); a 64-bit barrel shifter is 6 levels of 2:1 multiplexers.
in.core.alu.2.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11 (datapath subsystems: adders, shifters)

size.core.alu.statement: ALU: about 40 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: a 64-bit adder, shifter and logic unit
size.core.alu.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.core.muldiv.1.statement: Loop counts: a 64-bit multiply takes 8 iterations (4 for 32-bit), a divide 65 (33 for 32-bit); each multiply iteration Booth-encodes 4 partial products (4 x 2 bits = 8 multiplier bits).
in.core.muldiv.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.core.muldiv.statement: Multiplier and divider: about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.core.muldiv.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.core.csr.statement: Control and status registers: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.core.csr.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.vpu.statement: Vector unit: about 350 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. if it takes about half of a 0.25 mm2 minion, about 0.35 mm on a side (order of magnitude)
size.vpu.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.2.statement: RTL: vpu_lane, vpu_lane_tima, txfma_7s, tima, trans_unit, vpu_rf.
in.vpu.lane.2.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.vpu.lane.statement: Lane (one of eight): about 120 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. an eighth of the vector unit (order of magnitude)
size.vpu.lane.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.vrf.1.statement: The VRF: 64 entries x 32 bits (32 per thread), 3 read ports, 2 write ports (functional results and loads), thread ID as the address MSB, flopped inputs; "parameterized selection between ET-custom RF and synthesized SOL (sea-of-latches)".

in.vpu.lane.vrf.2.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.vpu.lane.vrf.3.statement: 8 lanes x 64 x 32 = 16,384 register bits per minion.

in.vpu.lane.vrf.4.statement: Which of the two register files (ET-custom or sea of latches) the ET-SoC-1 taped out is not stated.

size.vpu.lane.vrf.statement: Lane register file (64 x 32 bits, 3 read, 2 write ports): about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 2,048 bits with five ports: order of magnitude
size.vpu.lane.vrf.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.fma.1.statement: The TXFMA pipeline has 7 stages, the first used to clock-gate the operands when the unit is idle; it does 32-bit integer and FP32/FP16 arithmetic.

in.vpu.lane.fma.6.statement: A random-data 16x16x16 tile clocks 2.5 million register bits and toggles 74 million multiplier-tree nets; zeros clock nothing, because the lane clock is withheld when an operand word is zero.

size.vpu.lane.fma.statement: Fused multiply-add unit (TXFMA): about 60 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude; the multiplier array alone is some 20,000 transistors (see below)
size.vpu.lane.fma.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.fma.booth.1.statement: Partial-product generators txfma_booth_ppg_32r4 (radix 4, 32 bits) with a 17th partial product (booth_fpp17).
in.vpu.lane.fma.booth.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.vpu.lane.fma.booth.2.statement: 17 partial products of about 33 bits: some 560 partial-product bits, each a small multiplexer choosing 0, +/-1 or +/-2 times the multiplicand.
in.vpu.lane.fma.booth.2.source: arithmetic on the RTL's 17 radix-4 partial products

in.vpu.lane.fma.booth.3.statement: Radix-4 (modified) Booth recoding halves the partial products.
in.vpu.lane.fma.booth.3.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11 (datapath subsystems: multiplication)

size.vpu.lane.fma.booth.statement: Booth encoders and partial products: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.vpu.lane.fma.booth.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.fma.tree.1.statement: Modules txfma_wallace1, txfma_wallace2, txfma_4_2_compressor_array, txfma_4_2_compressor, txfma_csa.
in.vpu.lane.fma.tree.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.vpu.lane.fma.tree.2.statement: Reducing 17 rows of about 33 bits to 2 takes on the order of 500 full-adder equivalents; at about 28 transistors per full adder, some 14,000 transistors, about 20,000 with the Booth selectors.
in.vpu.lane.fma.tree.2.source: estimate from the RTL's structure and the textbook full adder (J. Rabaey, A. Chandrakasan, B. Nikolic, Digital Integrated Circuits, 2nd ed. (Prentice Hall 2003), ch. 11)

size.vpu.lane.fma.tree.statement: Compressor tree (Wallace tree of 4:2 compressors): about 40 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.vpu.lane.fma.tree.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.fma.norm.1.statement: Modules txfma_align_shf (alignment shifter), txfma_adder, txfma_lxd (leading-digit detection), txfma_norm_shf (normalisation shifter), txfma_rnd_adder (rounding adder), txfma_exp_special_detect.
in.vpu.lane.fma.norm.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.vpu.lane.fma.norm.statement: Align, add, normalise, round: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.vpu.lane.fma.norm.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.tima.3.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.vpu.lane.tima.statement: Integer multiply-add units (two TIMA): about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.vpu.lane.tima.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.lane.trans.1.statement: Every transcendental is a quadratic approximation of the mantissa, m1 = c0 + c1 x m0 + c2 x m0^2: the coefficients sit in ROMs ("LUT latch-based") addressed by the input mantissa's bits, and a sequencer runs the arithmetic as micro-instructions on the lane's TXFMA; the ROM unit has 7 stages like the TXFMA.
in.vpu.lane.trans.1.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf, pdf p.35 (§2.2.6) and p.61 (§2.3.7)

in.vpu.lane.trans.2.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.vpu.lane.trans.statement: Transcendental unit (exp2, log2, reciprocal): about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.vpu.lane.trans.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.vpu.shsw.1.statement: Stage F2 holds the TXFMA, the short-swizzle (SH-SW) unit, the mask and the transcendental sequencer; a bypass network forwards results from stages F3-F8 to the EX-stage inputs.

size.vpu.shsw.statement: Shuffle, swizzle and bypass network: about 80 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.vpu.shsw.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.tensor.4.statement: "A single tensor instruction can perform up to 32,000 operations"; tensor instructions "run for up to 512 cycles"; the integer pipeline sleeps meanwhile.
in.tensor.4.source: D. Ditzel et al., "Accelerating ML Recommendation With Over 1,000 RISC-V/Tensor Processors on Esperanto's ET-SoC-1 Chip", IEEE Micro 42(3), May/June 2022 (https://www.esperanto.ai/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Dave-IEEE-Micro.pdf), pp. 33-34

size.tensor.statement: Tensor sequencer: about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: state machines and two 1 KiB buffers
size.tensor.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.tensor.fsm.1.statement: Modules vpu_tensorfma, vpu_tensorquant, vpu_tensorreduce, vpu_ml, vpu_uinst_decoder.
in.tensor.fsm.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.tensor.fsm.statement: Tensor state machines: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.tensor.fsm.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.tensor.tenb.2.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.tensor.tenb.statement: TenB (stream buffer for B): about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. logically 1 KiB, "physically much smaller"
size.tensor.tenb.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.tensor.tenc.2.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.tensor.tenc.statement: TenC (int32 accumulators): about 40 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 8,192 bits of register file: order of magnitude

size.l1d.statement: L1 data cache (4 KB): about 120 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 32,768 latch bits at roughly 0.15-0.25 um2 each with their read trees is 0.005-0.008 mm2 (70-90 um), plus tags and TLB: order of magnitude
size.l1d.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.meta.statement: Tags, valid and LRU bits: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: 2,240 latch bits and 320 flip-flops
size.l1d.meta.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.cmp.statement: Tag comparators (four): about 10 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 33 XNORs and an AND tree each: about 10 um (order of magnitude)
size.l1d.cmp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.tlb.statement: TLB (8 entries): about 20 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.l1d.tlb.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.mh.statement: Miss handlers and replay queue: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.l1d.mh.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.data.statement: Data array (4 LRAM blocks): about 90 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. as the L1 minus its tags (order of magnitude)
size.l1d.data.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.block.statement: LRAM block (128 x 64): about 45 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 8,192 latch bits (order of magnitude)
size.l1d.block.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1d.row.statement: Row and read tree: about 32 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 64 latches of about 0.5 um: about 32 um long (inference)
size.l1d.row.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.l1scp.statement: L1 tensor scratchpad (3 KB): about 70 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. 12 of the L1's 16 sets (order of magnitude)
size.l1scp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.etlink.4.statement: ET-Link has a request and a reply channel, each handshaken by valid/ready pairs; a transfer happens only when both are high.

size.etlink.statement: ET-Link port: about 50 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: interface registers of 256-bit buses
size.etlink.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.fln.statement: Fast local network: about 500 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. its edges join minions a minion-width or two apart: about 0.5 mm (inference)
size.fln.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.master.statement: Master shire and spare shire: about 3.72 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. one tile pitch (chip.hop-pitch)
size.master.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.memshire.statement: Memory shire: about 3.7 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. a cell of the 1.76 mm side strip (L09), and, if the four memory shires of a side sit in the four middle rows as their mesh stops do, one tile pitch tall: about 1.8 x 3.7 mm
size.memshire.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.memshire.noc.statement: NoC port and clock crossing: about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.memshire.noc.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.memshire.ctrl.statement: Memory controllers (two uMCTL2): about 500 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.memshire.ctrl.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.memshire.phy.statement: DDR PHY (one for both channels): about 1 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. along the die edge in the 1.76 mm strip; order of magnitude
size.memshire.phy.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.memshire.phy.dq.statement: One DQ pin driver: about 20 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a pin driver's transistors are wide (tens of fins): tens of um (inference)
size.memshire.phy.dq.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.dram.statement: LPDDR4X package (memory chips): about 12 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. the card's part is not identified (dram.org.part); LPDDR4X packages are commonly about 10-15 mm on a side (inference)
size.dram.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.dram.chan.statement: Channel (one DRAM die or die pair): about 7 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. a DRAM die is several mm on a side; order of magnitude
size.dram.chan.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.dram.bank.statement: Bank and subarrays: about 2 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.dram.bank.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.dram.cell.statement: DRAM cell and sense amplifier: about 100 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. DRAM cells are tens of nm apart, their capacitors far taller; order of magnitude only
size.dram.cell.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.pcie.statement: PCIe shire: about 3.72 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. one tile pitch (chip.hop-pitch)
size.pcie.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.pcie.ctrl.statement: PCIe controllers (two): about 1 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.pcie.ctrl.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.pcie.phy.3.statement: A PCIe Gen4 lane carries 16 GT/s with 128b/130b encoding: 8 lanes give 8 x 16 x 128/130 / 8 = 15.75 GB/s per direction.
in.pcie.phy.3.source: PCI Express Base Specification 4.0 (16 GT/s, 128b/130b encoding); arithmetic as pcie.negotiated

size.pcie.phy.statement: PCIe PHY (8 lanes): about 2 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. along the die edge; order of magnitude
size.pcie.phy.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.pcie.lane.1.statement: A multi-gigabit lane: a serialiser and driver (with pre-emphasis) on the transmit side; on the receive side a continuous-time linear equaliser, decision-feedback equaliser, clock-and-data recovery and a deserialiser, clocked by a shared PLL.
in.pcie.lane.1.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 13 (I/O and high-speed links); no ET source describes the PHY's circuits

size.pcie.lane.statement: One SerDes lane: about 250 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.pcie.lane.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.io.statement: I/O shire: about 3.72 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. one tile pitch (chip.hop-pitch)
size.io.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.io.maxion.2.statement: An out-of-order core renames registers, holds decoded instructions in issue queues, executes them when their operands are ready and retires them in order from a reorder buffer.
in.io.maxion.2.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011) and standard texts; no ET source describes the ET-Maxion's microarchitecture

size.io.maxion.statement: ET-Maxion cores (four): about 600 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude; out-of-order cores are larger than minions
size.io.maxion.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.io.sp.statement: Service processor: about 500 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a minion core without vector unit, plus ROM and 1 MB SRAM (order of magnitude)
size.io.sp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.io.pll.1.statement: PLL0: I/O shire core clocks; PLL1: fixed high-frequency device clocks; PLL2: the NoC clock; PLL4: a stepping clock for the minions.
in.io.pll.1.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.429

size.io.pll.statement: Clock generators (PLL0-PLL4): about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a PLL is on the order of 0.01-0.05 mm2 (inference)
size.io.pll.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.io.pvt.1.statement: 36 process detectors and 36 temperature sensors (one each per minion shire and the I/O shire) and 8 voltage-monitor blocks of up to 16 sense points (128 in all), read through five PVT controllers. (The manual's own count does not add up: 34 minion shires and the I/O shire make 35, and it does not say where the 36th sensor sits.)
in.io.pvt.1.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17-18 (§1.6, Table 1-6: "36 sensors. 1 PD in each minion/IO-Shire")

size.io.pvt.statement: PVT controllers (five): about 100 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.io.pvt.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.io.periph.statement: Peripherals, root of trust, 4 MB cache: about 1 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.io.periph.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.mesh.7.statement: "Shires are connected to each other via an on-chip mesh interconnect operated on its own low-voltage domain."
in.mesh.7.source: D. Ditzel et al., "Accelerating ML Recommendation With Over 1,000 RISC-V/Tensor Processors on Esperanto's ET-SoC-1 Chip", IEEE Micro 42(3), May/June 2022 (https://www.esperanto.ai/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Dave-IEEE-Micro.pdf), p. 35

size.mesh.statement: The mesh (network on chip): about 22.2 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. the 6-column shire grid spans about 22.2 mm (L08); with the memory shires the mesh spans the die
size.mesh.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.mesh.link.4.statement: Measured on the mesh rail, routers included: 0.50-0.84 pF of switched capacitance per mm of travel, against 0.2-0.4 pF/mm estimated for a plain 7 nm repeated wire; most of the mesh's efficiency comes from its 0.485 V.

size.mesh.link.statement: One hop's link: about 3.72 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. one tile pitch long (chip.hop-pitch)
size.mesh.link.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.mesh.link.wire.statement: A wire segment between repeaters: about 200 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. repeaters every few hundred um (textbook); no ET source gives the spacing
size.mesh.link.wire.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.die.power.statement: Power delivery (rails, grid, bumps): about 25.7 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. spans the die
size.die.power.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.die.clock.statement: Clock distribution: about 25.7 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. spans the die
size.die.clock.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.die.metal.2.statement: TSMC N7: minimum metal pitch 40 nm (M0-M4, self-aligned double patterning).
in.die.metal.2.source: Wikipedia, "7 nm process", comparison table, row TSMC N7 (gate pitch 57 nm, fin pitch 30 nm, minimum metal pitch 40 nm, 91.2-96.5 MTr/mm2, SRAM cell 0.027 um2; fins SAQP, gates and M0-M4 SADP), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_nm_process (read 30 Sep 2026)

size.die.metal.statement: The wiring stack (metal layers): about 5 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a cross-section of the stack: a few um thick (inference; TSMC does not publish N7's stack heights)
size.die.metal.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.host.statement: The host computer: about 45 cm across (an estimate). An open frame holding an ATX board (30.5 x 24.4 cm) and its power supply: about 45 cm across (estimate from the photo; the frames' make is not recorded).
size.host.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

in.lib.inverter.1.statement: A static CMOS inverter is one PMOS and one NMOS transistor; energy per 0-to-1 output transition is about C x V^2.
in.lib.inverter.1.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 1, 2 and 5

in.lib.inverter.2.statement: TSMC N7 high-density cells are 240 nm tall (6 tracks of 40 nm); high-performance cells 300 nm.
in.lib.inverter.2.source: WikiChip Fuse, "TSMC 7nm HD and HP Cells, 2nd Gen 7nm, And The Snapdragon 855 DTCO", https://fuse.wikichip.org/?p=2408 (HD cell 240 nm tall = 6 tracks of 40 nm, HP 300 nm; about 91.2 MTr/mm2 HD, 65 HP); values as the search summary reported them, the page itself refused the connection on 30 Sep 2026
in.lib.inverter.2.note: Read from a search engine's summary of the page, which refused the connection; not yet re-read, so shown as inferred.

size.lib.inverter.statement: Inverter (NOT gate): about 240 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 2 gate pitches (114 nm) wide in a 240 nm-tall N7 high-density cell (inference from WikiChip Fuse)
size.lib.inverter.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.nand2.1.statement: A static CMOS 2-input NAND is 4 transistors.
in.lib.nand2.1.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 1

size.lib.nand2.statement: NAND gate: about 240 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 3 gate pitches wide in a 240 nm cell (inference)
size.lib.nand2.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.xor.1.statement: A static CMOS XOR takes about 8-12 transistors depending on style.
in.lib.xor.1.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 9 (combinational circuits)

size.lib.xor.statement: XOR / XNOR gate: about 300 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 5 gate pitches wide (inference)
size.lib.xor.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.mux2.1.statement: A 2:1 multiplexer is two transmission gates (4 transistors) plus an inverter, or about 12 transistors in static CMOS.
in.lib.mux2.1.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 9 (combinational circuits)

size.lib.mux2.statement: Two-way multiplexer: about 300 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 4-5 gate pitches wide (inference)
size.lib.mux2.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.arbiter.1.statement: The ET library has priority, LRU and round-robin arbiters (arb_prio, arb_lru, arb_rr, rr_sel).
in.lib.arbiter.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

size.lib.arbiter.statement: Arbiter: about 2 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: a few dozen gates
size.lib.arbiter.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.fa.1.statement: A static CMOS full adder takes about 28 transistors (the "mirror adder": 24 plus two output inverters).
in.lib.fa.1.source: J. Rabaey, A. Chandrakasan, B. Nikolic, Digital Integrated Circuits, 2nd ed. (Prentice Hall 2003), ch. 11 (arithmetic building blocks); N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11

size.lib.fa.statement: Full adder: about 800 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 12-16 gate pitches wide (inference)
size.lib.fa.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.cmp42.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.lib.cmp42.2.statement: A 4:2 compressor is equivalent to two full adders in series.
in.lib.cmp42.2.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11 (multiplication)

size.lib.cmp42.statement: 4:2 compressor: about 1.5 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. about two full adders (inference)
size.lib.cmp42.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.booth.1.statement: txfma_booth_ppg_32r4_norm decodes each 3-bit group into one of five selections (0, +1, +2, -2, -1).
in.lib.booth.1.note: Erbium RTL: core-et's RTL is the Erbium branch, the same Minion core lineage as the ET-SoC-1 in a later configuration; that the ET-SoC-1 silicon matches it block for block is not confirmed.

in.lib.booth.2.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11 (multiplication)

size.lib.booth.statement: Booth encoder and partial-product selector: about 500 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude
size.lib.booth.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.adder.1.statement: Parallel-prefix adders (Kogge-Stone, Sklansky, Brent-Kung) compute carries in log2(N) levels of generate/propagate cells.
in.lib.adder.1.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 11 (addition)

size.lib.adder.statement: Fast (parallel-prefix) adder: about 30 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. a 64-bit adder: tens of um (order of magnitude)
size.lib.adder.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.latch.statement: Latch (drawn as the L1's storage cell): about 500 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 8-10 gate pitches wide in a 240 nm cell: about 0.1-0.15 um2 (inference)
size.lib.latch.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.flipflop.statement: Flip-flop (register bit): about 1 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 16-20 gate pitches wide (inference)
size.lib.flipflop.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.icg.statement: Clock gate (ICG): about 600 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 10 gate pitches wide (inference)
size.lib.icg.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.levelshift.statement: Level shifter: about 1 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: it needs both supplies nearby
size.lib.levelshift.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.sync.statement: Synchroniser (two flip-flops): about 2 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. two flip-flops (inference)
size.lib.sync.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.senseamp.statement: Sense amplifier: about 2 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. about 4 SRAM columns wide (inference)
size.lib.senseamp.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.sram6t.2.statement: TSMC N7 high-density 6T SRAM cell: 0.027 um2.

size.lib.sram6t.statement: 6T SRAM cell: about 240 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. 0.027 um2: 2 gate pitches (114 nm) x about 8 fin pitches (237 nm), if the macros use N7's high-density cell (inference)
size.lib.sram6t.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.sram8t.statement: Two-port register-file cell (8T): about 300 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. larger than the 6T cell (order of magnitude)
size.lib.sram8t.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

size.lib.dram1t1c.statement: DRAM cell (1T1C): about 100 nm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude (a DRAM process, not TSMC N7)
size.lib.dram1t1c.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

in.lib.wire.1.statement: TSMC N7 minimum metal pitch 40 nm.
in.lib.wire.1.source: Wikipedia, "7 nm process", comparison table, row TSMC N7 (gate pitch 57 nm, fin pitch 30 nm, minimum metal pitch 40 nm, 91.2-96.5 MTr/mm2, SRAM cell 0.027 um2; fins SAQP, gates and M0-M4 SADP), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_nm_process (read 30 Sep 2026)

in.lib.wire.2.statement: Most wires have about 0.2 fF/um of capacitance, nearly independent of the process generation.
in.lib.wire.2.source: D. Harris, "Interconnect RC" lecture (https://pages.hmc.edu/harris/class/hal/lect4.pdf), as quoted in SYNTHESIS.md line 160

in.lib.repeater.2.statement: Delay of an unrepeated wire grows with the square of its length; optimally spaced repeaters make it linear.
in.lib.repeater.2.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 6 (interconnect)

in.lib.clocktree.2.statement: The DLL compensates the variable delays in the distribution network of shire_clock and neigh_clock (voltage, temperature, process).
in.lib.clocktree.2.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Shire DLL Delay Control.pdf, pdf p.3 (§1)

in.lib.clocktree.3.statement: Clock distribution by H-trees, grids or spines of buffers.
in.lib.clocktree.3.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 13 (clocks, PLLs and DLLs)

size.lib.clocktree.statement: Clock tree: about 3.72 mm across, the width of the view that frames it. a shire's clock tree spans its tile

in.lib.finfet.1.statement: TSMC N7: FinFET, contacted gate pitch 57 nm, fin pitch 30 nm.
in.lib.finfet.1.source: Wikipedia, "7 nm process", comparison table, row TSMC N7 (gate pitch 57 nm, fin pitch 30 nm, minimum metal pitch 40 nm, 91.2-96.5 MTr/mm2, SRAM cell 0.027 um2; fins SAQP, gates and M0-M4 SADP), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_nm_process (read 30 Sep 2026)

in.lib.finfet.2.source: S.-Y. Wu et al. (TSMC), "A 7nm CMOS platform technology featuring 4th generation FinFET transistors with a 0.027um2 high density 6-T SRAM cell for mobile SoC applications", IEDM 2016, paper 2.6

in.lib.finfet.3.statement: N7 high-density cells are 240 nm tall; high-performance cells 300 nm.
in.lib.finfet.3.source: WikiChip Fuse, "TSMC 7nm HD and HP Cells, 2nd Gen 7nm, And The Snapdragon 855 DTCO", https://fuse.wikichip.org/?p=2408 (HD cell 240 nm tall = 6 tracks of 40 nm, HP 300 nm; about 91.2 MTr/mm2 HD, 65 HP); values as the search summary reported them, the page itself refused the connection on 30 Sep 2026
in.lib.finfet.3.note: Read from a search engine's summary of the page, which refused the connection; not yet re-read, so shown as inferred.

in.lib.gate.2.statement: Comparable generations: TSMC 10 nm minimum Lg about 25 nm; Intel 10 nm 18 nm.
in.lib.gate.2.source: D. James (Siliconics), "A Quick Look at 14-nm and 10-nm", AVS Joint Users Group, July 2018 (JTG718-4), slides 11 and 17-18: TSMC 10 nm (Apple A11) fin pitch ~33 nm, fin width ~6 nm, functional gate height ~44 nm, gate width ~95 nm; Intel 10 nm fin height 46-53 nm, width ~7 nm at half height, Lg 18 nm; https://nccavs-usergroups.avs.org/wp-content/uploads/JTG2018/JTG718-4-James-Siliconics.pdf

in.lib.gate.3.statement: A high-k metal gate: a hafnium-based oxide on a thin silicon-oxide interlayer under work-function metals; TSMC does not publish its N7 stack.
in.lib.gate.3.source: N. Weste and D. Harris, CMOS VLSI Design, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley 2011), ch. 3 (processing)

in.lib.fin.1.statement: TSMC N7 fin pitch 30 nm (self-aligned quadruple patterning).
in.lib.fin.1.source: Wikipedia, "7 nm process", comparison table, row TSMC N7 (gate pitch 57 nm, fin pitch 30 nm, minimum metal pitch 40 nm, 91.2-96.5 MTr/mm2, SRAM cell 0.027 um2; fins SAQP, gates and M0-M4 SADP), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_nm_process (read 30 Sep 2026)

in.lib.fin.2.statement: TSMC 10 nm (Apple A11): fin width ~6 nm, functional gate height ~44 nm; Intel 10 nm: fin height 46-53 nm, width ~7 nm at half height.
in.lib.fin.2.source: D. James (Siliconics), "A Quick Look at 14-nm and 10-nm", AVS Joint Users Group, July 2018 (JTG718-4), slides 11 and 17-18: TSMC 10 nm (Apple A11) fin pitch ~33 nm, fin width ~6 nm, functional gate height ~44 nm, gate width ~95 nm; Intel 10 nm fin height 46-53 nm, width ~7 nm at half height, Lg 18 nm; https://nccavs-usergroups.avs.org/wp-content/uploads/JTG2018/JTG718-4-James-Siliconics.pdf

in.lib.si.1.source: NIST CODATA 2018: lattice parameter of silicon a = 543.1020511 pm (at 22.5 C in vacuum), https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?asil

in.lib.si.2.statement: Diamond cubic: 8 atoms per cubic cell gives 8 / 0.5431^3 nm3 = 50 atoms per nm3 (5.0 x 10^22 per cm3); nearest neighbours are sqrt(3)/4 x a = 0.235 nm apart.

in.lib.si.3.statement: Across a 6 nm fin whose sidewalls are (110) planes (the usual orientation on a (100) wafer, an assumption), the (220) planes are a / sqrt(8) = 0.192 nm apart: about 31 planes of atoms.
in.lib.si.3.source: arithmetic on the lattice parameter, the inferred 6 nm fin and the assumed (110) sidewalls: inferred

size.fma.tree.col.statement: One column of the compressor tree: about 10 µm across, the width of the view that frames it. order of magnitude: one bit-column of a tree some 40 um wide
size.fma.tree.col.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/inside.json, size)

out.package.1.statement: A 45.0 x 45.0 mm flip-chip ball-grid array with a 44.8 mm lid, at most 3.95 mm tall, with 2,494 solder balls of 0.50 mm diameter.
out.package.1.source: Esperanto, ET-SoC-1 Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0 (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), Fig. 9-1, p. 33 (also the heatsink feasibility page, docs/reports/sources/esperanto-without-heatsink.body.html, section 1)

out.package.2.statement: Most balls sit on a 0.80 mm grid; the drawing also dimensions a central region at 0.90-0.96 mm spacing. Columns are numbered 1-53 and rows lettered A-BR (skipping I, O, Q, S, X, Z), with many positions left empty: 2,494 balls in all.
out.package.2.source: Esperanto, ET-SoC-1 Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0 (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), Fig. 9-1 (dimensions read off the bottom view)

out.package.3.statement: More than 30,000 bumps join the die to the package substrate: the substrate fans them out to the 2,494 balls, about 12 bumps per ball.
out.package.3.source: D. Ditzel, "Esperanto ET-SoC-1", Hot Chips 33 (2021), slides, as cited on the heatsink page (docs/reports/sources/esperanto-without-heatsink.body.html, section 1, ref [3])

out.package.4.statement: Under the lid: a die of 570 mm^2, about 25.6 x 22.2 mm. Where it sits under the lid is not documented; the drawing centres it.

out.package.5.statement: TSMC 7 nm, more than 24 billion transistors.

out.package.6.statement: The vendor photo's lid reads "ET-SoC-1 ... A0 ... 2217 ES TT TAIWAN": in the datasheet's scheme a date code (2217), an engineering sample (ES), assembled in Taiwan. "TT" is not explained there. The lab cards' own markings are not recorded.
out.package.6.source: Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), p. 2 (photo); Esperanto, ET-SoC-1 Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0 (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), Table 10-1, p. 34

out.package.7.statement: The datasheet gives no thermal ratings for the package (section 9.1 is a placeholder).

out.package.8.statement: Light crosses the die (25.6 mm) in 0.085 ns, about a twentieth of one 600 MHz clock tick; in one tick light goes 50 cm.
out.package.8.source: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI Brochure, 9th ed., 2019): c = 299 792 458 m/s exactly; the clock: docs/findings/14-card-behaviour.md:338

size.package.statement: The package: about 45 mm across. 45.0 x 45.0 mm body (datasheet Fig. 9-1, p. 33).
size.package.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

out.card.1.statement: 6.6 x 4.4 in (167.6 x 111.8 mm); a PCIe x16 card edge carrying an x8 PCIe Gen 4 link; the chip soldered down, no socket.
out.card.1.source: Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), pp. 1 and 3

out.card.2.statement: On all four lab cards the link runs at 16 GT/s on 8 lanes: 15.75 GB/s each way after coding. Measured host-to-card DMA: 12.5-12.6 GB/s; card to host 10.4-10.5 GB/s.
out.card.2.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-pcie/hosts.txt (the link speed and width of all four cards); docs/findings/05-claims.md:550-552 (E50: the DMA rates, on three cards)

out.card.3.statement: Four LPDDR4X memory packages, 256 bits wide in all (16 channels of 16 bits), 32 GB: each package serves two of the chip's eight memory shires.
out.card.3.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/facts.json (L47, dram.channels); Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), p. 1

out.card.4.statement: Peak memory rate on these cards: 256 bits x 3,733 MT/s = 119.5 GB/s, the firmware's 933 MHz mode, which every lab card runs; the datasheet's 4,266 MT/s would give 136.5 GB/s. Tensor loads from memory have been measured at 75 GB/s.
out.card.4.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/facts.json (dram.rate-card: the firmware hard-codes 3,733 MT/s on every card; dram.peak-card; L47: the datasheet's 4,266 Mb/s per pin); docs/findings/05-claims.md:155 (E15)

out.card.5.statement: Each memory package is about 15 mm square on the vendor photo, which shows SK hynix parts (a second photo in the same document shows Micron parts). Which maker's DRAM the lab cards carry is not recorded.
out.card.5.source: Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), pp. 2, 8 and 10 (photos)

out.card.6.statement: Power arrives as 12 V at the card edge: at most 7.3 A, 88 W. The highest draw on record is 87.8 W; the cards idle at about 19-36 W, depending on the card and its temperature.
out.card.6.source: Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), p. 5 (power tree); docs/findings/14-card-behaviour.md:138, 339
out.card.6.note: The statement combines spec, measured; it is labelled by the weakest, spec.

out.card.7.statement: The cores run at about 0.52 V at 600 MHz, 23 times lower than the 12 V input, so the current is about 23 times higher: a Texas Instruments TPSM831D31 supplies the cores (3 phases, up to 120 A) and the on-chip network (1 phase, 40 A). Its four phases are the four large inductors marked "R15" on the photo.
out.card.7.source: Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), p. 1 (key voltage regulators) and p. 2 (photo); docs/findings/05-claims.md:34 (E9)
out.card.7.note: The statement combines spec, measured, inferred; it is labelled by the weakest, inferred.

out.card.8.statement: An Analog Devices LTM4680 module (up to 60 A) supplies the SRAM rail; smaller FS1406 regulators the memory, PCIe, I/O and other rails; an LTC4218 hot-swap switch with a 1 mΩ sense resistor measures the card's input current for the power readings.

out.card.9.statement: A small microcontroller (Microchip ATSAMD20, the "PMIC micro") reads the 12 V input and three regulators (cores, network, SRAM); the other rails have set points only.
out.card.9.source: Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), p. 4 (block diagram); docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/facts.json (board.meters)
out.card.9.note: The statement combines spec, measured; it is labelled by the weakest, spec.

out.card.10.statement: Also on the board: 64 GB of eMMC flash (a Kingston part on the photo), an FTDI UART-to-USB bridge, JTAG, DIP switches that set the boot options, and a fan header (P1).
out.card.10.note: The statement combines spec, inferred; it is labelled by the weakest, inferred.

out.card.12.statement: A signal in the board's copper travels at about half the speed of light (c/√εr, εr ≈ 4 for FR-4), so crossing the card takes about 1.12 ns: two-thirds of a 600 MHz clock tick.
out.card.12.source: physics: a buried trace's delay is √εr / c; εr = 4 is ASSUMED (typical FR-4 is 3.8-4.5), so the result is inferred

size.card.statement: The PCIe card: about 16.8 cm across. 6.6 x 4.4 in (167.6 x 111.8 mm), the dev card's assembly drawing (p. 3).
size.card.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

out.host.1.statement: The lab's three hosts: aifoundry1, an Intel Core i7-11700K (8 cores) with 128 GB; aifoundry2, a Core i5-11600 (6 cores) with 64 GB; aifoundry3, an i7-11700K with 32 GB on a single memory channel.

out.host.2.statement: aifoundry2's motherboard is a Gigabyte Z590 AORUS MASTER, an ATX board of 30.5 x 24.4 cm. The other two hosts' BIOS versions (F5, F6) follow Gigabyte's naming, but their board models are not recorded.
out.host.2.source: the host's DMI table (/sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id, read 30 Sep 2026); Gigabyte, Z590 AORUS MASTER specifications (gigabyte.com); docs/findings/14-card-behaviour.md:348
out.host.2.note: The statement combines measured, spec, inferred; it is labelled by the weakest, inferred.

out.host.3.statement: aifoundry1 holds two ET cards, the other hosts one each.

out.host.4.statement: Each card's 8-lane PCIe 4.0 link goes straight to a root port on the CPU, which has 20 PCIe 4.0 lanes.
out.host.4.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-pcie/hosts.txt (root_port 00:01.x, the CPU's own PCIe ports on this platform: inferred); Intel, Core i7-11700K specifications (intel.com)
out.host.4.note: The statement combines measured, inferred, spec; it is labelled by the weakest, inferred.

out.host.5.statement: The host CPUs are made in Intel's 14 nm process; the i7-11700K is rated at 125 W base power and may draw up to 251 W in turbo (its PL2), the i5-11600 at 65 W base. The whole ET card, at most 88 W, draws less than the bigger CPU's base power, and about a third of its turbo peak.
out.host.5.source: Intel, Core i7-11700K and Core i5-11600 specifications (intel.com: 125 W and 65 W base power); the i7-11700K's 251 W maximum turbo power (PL2) as listed by cpu-monkey.com and techreviewer.com; Esperanto, "PCIe Dev Card (V3)", ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf (github.com/aifoundry-org/et-man), p. 5

out.host.6.statement: The host copies memory at 17.4 / 9.2 / 21.4 GB/s (aifoundry2 / 3 / 1); a program's staged copy to the card is limited by both that and the link: 5.2-7.8 GB/s.

out.host.7.statement: The owner's photo shows open-air frames with tower coolers and EVGA and MSI power supplies; several boards carry Gigabyte AORUS logos.

out.host.8.statement: A standard ATX power supply is 150 mm wide, 86 mm high and 140 mm deep.
out.host.8.source: Intel, ATX12V Power Supply Design Guide (version 2.x), physical dimensions of the standard ATX12V supply

out.rack.1.statement: About ten open-frame machines on two shelves, five to a shelf, some partly hidden.
out.rack.1.source: the owner's rack photo (30 Sep 2026), counted

out.rack.2.statement: The lab's machines are in this rack; which three of them is not recorded.

out.rack.3.statement: Power supplies read on the photo: EVGA 650 GS and 1000 GS, MSI MPG A750GF (650, 1,000 and 750 W).

out.rack.4.statement: A "KVM#8" label and a keyboard on the shelf above: one keyboard and screen are shared between machines.

out.rack.5.statement: Light crosses the rack in 5 ns, about 3 of the chip's clock ticks at 600 MHz.
out.rack.5.source: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI Brochure, 9th ed., 2019): c = 299 792 458 m/s exactly

size.rack.statement: The rack: about 1.5 m across (an estimate). About 1.5 m wide: five open frames side by side on each shelf (estimate from the photo; common wire-shelving widths are 48-72 in). The rack's make and size are not recorded.
size.rack.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

out.localgroup.3.statement: The Triangulum galaxy (M33), the third largest member, is about 3 million light-years away; the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite of ours, about 160,000.
out.localgroup.3.source: NASA, Hubble Messier catalogue, M33; NASA APOD, 28 May 2013 (the Large Cloud of Magellan)

out.localgroup.4.statement: A collision with Andromeda, long predicted for about 4.5 billion years from now, now looks about a coin flip within 10 billion years, and under 2% within 5 billion.
out.localgroup.4.source: T. Sawala et al., Nature Astronomy (2025), "No certainty of a Milky Way-Andromeda collision"

out.localgroup.5.statement: More than 130 members are now known within a megaparsec of the group's centre (134 in one count), most of them faint dwarf galaxies; counted that way the group is about 5.1 Mpc (17 million light-years) across.
out.localgroup.5.source: Wikipedia, "Local Group" (read 1 Oct 2026): "a current total of 134 members is known within 1 megaparsec", "most of which are dwarf galaxies", "a total diameter of 5.11 megaparsecs (17 million light-years)"

out.localgroup.6.statement: A galaxy cluster is far larger than a group: the nearest big one, the Virgo Cluster, about 54 million light-years away, has about 1,300 (possibly up to 2,000) galaxies. The Local Group belongs to the Virgo Supercluster, which is part of Laniakea.
out.localgroup.6.source: Wikipedia, "Virgo Cluster" and "Local Group" (read 1 Oct 2026); Tully et al. 2014 (Laniakea, below)

size.localgroup.statement: The Local Group (Andromeda): about 10 million light-years across. Its galaxies are spread over a diameter of nearly 10 million light-years (NASA).
size.localgroup.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

out.laniakea.1.statement: A region about 160 Mpc (520 million light-years) across, holding about 10^17 times the Sun's mass, defined by where galaxies' motions flow inward; "lani" means heaven and "akea" spacious, immeasurable.
out.laniakea.1.source: R. B. Tully, H. Courtois, Y. Hoffman, D. Pomarède, "The Laniakea supercluster of galaxies", Nature 513, 71-73 (2014), arXiv:1409.0880

size.laniakea.statement: Laniakea: about 522 million light-years across. 160 Mpc across if taken as round (Tully et al. 2014): 522 million light-years.
size.laniakea.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

out.universe.1.statement: Age 13.79 billion years by these parameters (Planck 2018: 13.787 ± 0.020).
out.universe.1.source: Planck Collaboration, "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters", A&A 641, A6 (2020), Table 2

out.universe.2.source: derived from the Planck 2018 parameters (this script)

out.universe.3.statement: The oldest light we can see, the cosmic microwave background, left its source about 380,000 years after the Big Bang; it now has a temperature of 2.7255 K.
out.universe.3.source: NASA/WMAP Science Team (the nine-year map's caption); D. J. Fixsen, ApJ 707, 916 (2009)

out.universe.4.statement: The observable universe is about 3 × 10^28 times wider than the chip's 25.6 mm die.

size.universe.statement: The observable universe: about 92.4 billion light-years across. Twice the comoving distance to the particle horizon: 14.16 Gpc = 46.2 billion ly radius, from Planck 2018's parameters (H0 67.66, Ωm 0.3111, ΩΛ 0.6889, radiation from T = 2.7255 K, Neff 3.046).
size.universe.source: the deep zoom's scale ladder (research/outside.json, size_m and size_note)

out.beyond.1.statement: Measured space is flat to within a fraction of a percent (Ω_K = 0.001 ± 0.002), which suggests the universe extends well past the observable part.

out.beyond.2.statement: One analysis puts the whole universe at more than 251 times the volume of our Hubble sphere (99% level), under its model assumptions.
out.beyond.2.source: M. Vardanyan, R. Trotta, J. Silk, "Applications of Bayesian model averaging to the curvature and size of the Universe", MNRAS 413, L91-L95 (2011), arXiv:1101.5476

out.beyond.3.statement: Eternal inflation and the string-theory "landscape" suggest many separate universes. Nothing observed so far confirms or rules this out.
out.beyond.3.source: A. H. Guth, "Eternal inflation and its implications", J. Phys. A 40, 6811 (2007), arXiv:hep-th/0702178

ml:dram:dram.addr.addrmap.statement: The controllers' address map as programmed (ECC off): column bits 4:0 = HIF 4:0, bank bits 2:0 = HIF 7:5, column bits 9:5 = HIF 12:8, row bits 16:0 = HIF 29:13 (HIF is the controller's internal address in 16-bit words).
ml:dram:dram.addr.addrmap.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4639-4654 (ADDRMAP1 0x00030303, ADDRMAP2 0x03000000, ADDRMAP3 0x03030303, ADDRMAP5-6 0x07070707, ADDRMAP7 0x00000f07); field meanings and internal bases from external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html (ADDRMAP1-7); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md §3.4
ml:dram:dram.addr.addrmap.note: Register values are from the firmware source; the running cards' registers have not been read back (the hub's ask-memshire). The 32 GB ECC branch (:4590-4626) is not taken: ECC is off.

ml:dram:dram.addr.channel.statement: Inside the memory shire, physical-address bit 9 picks the controller (the channel): the memory shire's control register resets with its controller-select bit field at 9 and both controllers enabled, and the default boot never rewrites it. The two channels alternate every 512 bytes.
ml:dram:dram.addr.channel.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:22 (`MEMSHIRE_MCTL_SEL_ADDR_RANGE 9`); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/ms_regs.h:160 (MS_REGS_MS_MEM_CTL_RESET_VALUE 0x000307f1892481c6: esr_ms_addr_mc_bit_sel = 9, esr_ms_mc_en = 3; fields at ms_regs.h:489-600); external/core-et/rtl/inc/esr_defines.vh:149-158 (ESR_MS_MEM_CTL_RESET_VAL); only the reduced-memory-shire path writes ms_mem_ctl (external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/noc_configuration.c:294-313); zebumem.c:72 ('addr[9] controller (0=even, 1=odd)')
ml:dram:dram.addr.channel.note: Upgrades the earlier inference from a tool comment (counters-and-dram.md §3.4, chip-diagram fact L50): the reset value is in the SoC's own register header. Latency cannot see this bit: flipping it, like flipping a bank bit, lets the second load ride along (memprobe summary.json bits['9'].b_minus_b0_med = 0).

ml:dram:dram.addr.pa-map.statement: In physical-address terms, inside one channel: bank = PA[12:10] (8 banks), column = PA[17:13] and PA[5:1] (1,024 columns of 16 bits, a 2 KB page), row = PA[34:18] (17 bits). A 64-byte line is two 32-byte BL16 bursts from one row; PA[5] picks the half.
ml:dram:dram.addr.pa-map.source: derived from dram.addr.strip and dram.addr.addrmap (HIF = controller byte address / 2 for a 16-bit channel); measured by flipping one bit: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json bits['13'..'17'].b_minus_b0_med = -12 (same row), bits['18'..'29'] = +9 (other row), bits['6'..'12'] ~ 0; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P4; anatomy page §5 #which-address-bits-share-a-row; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md §3.4
ml:dram:dram.addr.pa-map.note: Bank and row bits are measured (a same-bank, other-row pair conflicts from bit 18 up on three cards); the split of PA[12:10] into bank rather than channel or column is from the programmed map. zebumem.c:74-111 prints a different swizzle, but only 'if using DDR DRAM models' (an emulation model), and silicon disagrees with it.

ml:dram:dram.addr.strip.statement: Before a request reaches its controller, the memory shire removes physical-address bits 9:6 (the memory-shire and channel bits), so each controller sees its own lines as one contiguous address space.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.RL-WL.statement: Read latency RL = 18 DFI clocks = 36 DRAM clocks = 19.3 ns (read DBI on); write latency WL = 8 DFI = 16 DRAM clocks = 8.6 ns.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.atomic-unit.statement: The memory shire contains an atomic unit with a small atomic cache (ms_atomic_sm_ctl bits 7:4 flag which entries hold dirty data; a 4-bit state), and the datasheet lists 'LPDDR4X support for global atomic operations'.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.atomic-unit.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 Table 15-90 (ms_atomic_sm_ctl); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:121 (`MEMSHIRE_ATOMIC_STATE_SIZE 4`), :268-271 (memshire atomics); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1
ml:dram:dram.ctl.atomic-unit.note: When a global atomic on a DRAM address is done here rather than at the L3 home is not documented (ask).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.burst.statement: Burst length 16 on a 16-bit channel: one READ returns 32 bytes in 8 DRAM clocks (4.3 ns, tCCD = 4 DFI clocks), so a 64-byte line takes two READs to the same row.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.cam.statement: The controller's transaction store (CAM) gives 32 entries to low-priority reads (SCHED.lpr_num_entries = 0x1f, 'this value + 1'); the total depth, a build parameter, is not in the sources.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.clock.statement: The firmware hard-codes the '933 MHz' DDR mode on every card: the controller (DFI) clock is 933 MHz and runs 1:2 with the DRAM clock, so the DRAM clock is 1,866 MHz and the data rate 3,733 MT/s, not the datasheet's 4,266. Telemetry reads mhz.ddr = 933 in every sample.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.clock.source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:643-649 (DDR_FREQUENCY_933MHZ, '//TODO: decide ddr_mode'); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:768 (DfiFreqRatio_p0=1), :4536 (MSTR 0x00080020: lpddr4=1, burst_rdwr=8 = BL16); docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace2-telemetry.jsonl field mhz.ddr
ml:dram:dram.ctl.clock.note: One DFI clock = 1.071 ns, one DRAM clock tCK = 0.536 ns; timings below convert DFI clocks to ns. At 600 MHz one minion cycle is 1.667 ns.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.dbi.statement: Data-bus inversion is on for reads and writes, and data masking is enabled: the controller's DBICTL sets rd_dbi_en, wr_dbi_en and dm_en.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.dbi.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4522 (DBICTL 0x7: rd_dbi_en=1, wr_dbi_en=1, dm_en=1), :4398 (INIT4 emr2=0xf1 = MR3); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:322
ml:dram:dram.ctl.dbi.note: The init also writes MR3 = 0xF1 (INIT4.emr2). In LPDDR4 (GENERIC) MR3 holds PU-CAL, PDDS and the DBI-RD/WR enables, and data masking is set by MR13 OP[5].

ml:dram:dram.ctl.dfi-update.statement: The controller requests DFI controller updates (PHY re-trims) automatically every 64-255 x 1,024 DFI clocks (70-280 us).
ml:dram:dram.ctl.dfi-update.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4528-4531 (DFIUPD0 dis_auto_ctrlupd=0; DFIUPD1 interval min 64, max 255 x1024); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:333
ml:dram:dram.ctl.dfi-update.note: That these cause rare latency blips is an inference (counters-and-dram.md), not measured.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.measured-bw.statement: Streaming from DRAM the whole chip reaches 76 GB/s at 600 MHz (64% of 119.5); tensor stores to DRAM also reach 76 GB/s, stores through the L1 27 GB/s.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.measured-bw.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'Bandwidth at 600 MHz, 1,024 minions' (E33, E29); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table rows 'Tensor load from DRAM', 'fsw.ps stores to DRAM through the L1'

ml:dram:dram.ctl.page-policy.statement: Open-page policy: the controller keeps a bank's row open until it must close it (another row of that bank, or a refresh); no page-close timer, no auto-precharge.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.page-policy.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4661-4664 (SCHED 0x00a01f01: pageclose=0; SCHED1 pageclose_timer=0), :4668 (PCCFG 0); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:245 (config_auto_precharge = 0); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 (ddrc_main_ctl: read/write auto-precharge, high/low priority); meaning of pageclose=0 from external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html (SCHED.pageclose: 'the bank remains open until there is a need to close it ... also known as open page policy')
ml:dram:dram.ctl.page-policy.note: Measured: 96% of loads whose previous load came after the last refresh were row hits, 4% across a refresh (anatomy §5; 95-96% vs 3-4% on three cards).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.peak-bw.statement: At 3,733 MT/s a 16-bit channel peaks at 7.47 GB/s, a memory shire at 14.9 GB/s and the chip at 119.5 GB/s; at the datasheet's 4,266 MT/s the chip would reach 136.5 GB/s.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.peak-bw.source: arithmetic: 2 B x 3.733 GT/s; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.4 §1 (4,266 MT/s, printed '133 Gbytes/s')

ml:dram:dram.ctl.perfmon.statement: Each memory shire has a perf monitor (40-bit cycle counter at 933 MHz and two event counters).
