The firmware sets them to count mesh reads and writes, which a user kernel can sample through syscall 10; the same monitor can count controller commands (activate, precharge, refresh, per bank), but only M-mode can select that and the encodings are in a document not in the sources.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.perfmon.source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:381-418 (§3.5); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:215-250 (MCOP qualifier: cmd bits 14:0, bank bits 27:20; MESHCNT qualifier)
ml:dram:dram.ctl.perfmon.note: Hub rungs 13-14 and the missing 'Memory Shire Specification §5.4.22-29'.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.ports.statement: Each controller has two AXI ports with aging on: port 0 at priority 15 (commented 'lower priority') and port 1 at priority 8 ('higher priority'), for reads and writes alike; the memory shire keeps high/low request lines per controller, and the shire cache marks its to-memory requests high or low QoS from an ESR.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.ports.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4670-4680 (PCFGR_0 0x100f, PCFGR_1 0x1008, PCFGW_0 0x100f, PCFGW_1 0x1008); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:95 (`MEMSHIRE_WRITE_CNT_SIZE`, 'one per priority'); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_types.vh (ddrc_esr_ctl_t: u0/u1 csysreq_hi/lo); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.97 §4.1 (esr_sc_axi_qos: AXI_QOS_MEM_HIGH_PRIORITY / _LOW_PRIORITY)
ml:dram:dram.ctl.ports.note: Which traffic is steered to which port, and what esr_sc_axi_qos is set to, is not in the sources (ask).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.power-down.statement: No power-down and no self-refresh: the firmware disables both 'for performance reasons', so an idle channel stays in active standby with its clocks running.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.power-down.note: GENERIC consequence: the DRAM's active-standby current flows whenever the card is up; its share of the idle 12-18 W unmetered power is unattributed (hub §4.2).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.refresh-mode.statement: All-bank refresh every tREFI = 113 x 32 = 3,616 DFI clocks = 3.875 us, each taking tRFCab = 262 DFI clocks = 280.7 ns; per-bank refresh off; temperature derating not enabled.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.refresh-mode.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4441 (RFSHCTL0 0x00210000: per_bank_refresh=0), :4443 (RFSHTMG 0x80710106: t_rfc_nom_x1_x32=0x71, t_rfc_min=0x106), :5475 (RFSHCTL3=0: auto-refresh on after init), :4686-4688 (DERATEEN commented out: 'FUTURE derate is not needed for bring-up'); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html RFSHTMG.t_rfc_nom_x1_sel ('for ... per-bank refresh only'; unit 'multiples of 32 DFI clock cycles')
ml:dram:dram.ctl.refresh-mode.note: counters-and-dram.md §3.2 had to guess the x32 reading because t_rfc_nom_x1_sel=1; the uMCTL2 register description says x1_sel applies only to per-bank refresh, and the measured period (dram.lat.refresh-period) confirms x32.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.scheduling.statement: The scheduler serves up to 15 transactions of one kind (high-priority reads, low-priority reads, writes) before switching when another kind waits; low-priority reads and writes may be starved at most 127 clocks, high-priority reads 1.
ml:dram:dram.ctl.scheduling.note: Field meanings are the uMCTL2 register names (xact_run_length, max_starve); the scheduler's algorithm itself is Synopsys's and GENERIC here.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.tRAS-tRC.statement: Minimum row-open time tRAS = 40 DFI clocks = 42.9 ns; row cycle tRC (activate to activate in one bank) = 59 DFI clocks = 63.2 ns (37.9 cycles).
ml:dram:dram.ctl.tRAS-tRC.note: tRC matches the measured back-to-back row-conflict penalty (+36.5 to +38.5 cycles, dram.lat.row-conflict).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.tRCD.statement: Activate-to-read delay tRCD = 17 DFI clocks = 18.2 ns (10.9 minion cycles at 600 MHz).
ml:dram:dram.ctl.tRCD.note: Measured: an open-row hit saves 11-12 cycles (dram.lat.row-hit).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.tRP.statement: Precharge time tRP = 17 DFI clocks = 18.2 ns (10.9 cycles).
ml:dram:dram.ctl.tRP.note: Measured: a load to another row of the bank just used pays about 9-10 cycles more (dram.lat.row-sequential).

ml:dram:dram.ctl.tWR.statement: Write recovery: MR1 = 0x64 sets nWR = 34 DRAM clocks (18.2 ns); write-to-precharge wr2pre = 30 DFI clocks, read-to-precharge rd2pre = 8.

ml:dram:dram.ctl.zq.statement: Automatic ZQ calibration (the periodic re-trim of the DRAM's output-driver and termination impedance) is disabled.

ml:dram:dram.e.data.statement: Even DRAM is data-dependent: a tensor load from DRAM costs 94.6 pJ/B on zeros [86.2-105.7] and 132.6 on random data [117.9-145.4]; a tensor store 94.4 and 141.9.
ml:dram:dram.e.data.note: With read and write DBI on and LVSTL I/O terminated to ground (GENERIC), driving ones costs current and zeros almost none; that is one plausible share of the gap, not measured separately.

ml:dram:dram.e.per-byte.statement: Reading DRAM costs 114.6 pJ per byte above idle [89.0-141.3 over 18 passes] with 1 KB tensor loads at 600 MHz (aifoundry2 111.5, aifoundry3 105.6, aifoundry1-c1 126.6): about 7.3 nJ per 64-byte line.
ml:dram:dram.e.per-byte.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json reruns.levels_pj_per_byte['dram'] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table row 'DRAM'

ml:dram:dram.e.rows.statement: The DRAM row pattern does not change the energy per byte: row hits 155.9, row misses 158.5, sequential 156.4 pJ/B on random data (120.4 / 118.5 / 120.6 on zeros), indistinguishable on every card; an activation costing 30 pJ/B on zeros or 50 on random data would have shown.
ml:dram:dram.e.rows.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['dramrow2/rowhit/random'], ['dramrow2/rowmiss/random'], ['dramrow2/seq/random'] (and /zeros); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md '## Rows: does the DRAM row pattern matter?'; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM row walks (seq, rowhit, rowmiss) over a DRAM tensor load' (E45)
ml:dram:dram.e.rows.note: The manual's caveat: with 32 streams interleaved and a refresh every 2,325 cycles, every pattern may have paid an activation; so the activate energy is bounded, not measured. Per 64-byte line the bound is ~1.9 nJ (zeros) to ~3.2 nJ (random).

ml:dram:dram.e.split-unknown.statement: How the ~73 pJ/B off-rail DRAM energy splits between the memory shires' logic, the PHY's I/O, the DRAM core (activate, sensing, column path) and the DRAM's own I/O is not measurable on the card: none of those rails has a current sensor.
ml:dram:dram.e.split-unknown.source: docs/findings/19-observability-and-the-unmetered.md ('The other rails — DDR core 0.8 V, VDDQ 1.1 V, VDDQLP ... have set points in the PMIC and no telemetry'); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52, 255

ml:dram:dram.e.unmetered.statement: About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail: a DRAM tensor load splits 2% minion cores, 11% SRAM, 18% mesh, 69% unmetered; the fit of the unmetered remainder puts 72.7 (aifoundry2), 72.7 (aifoundry3) and 81.6 (aifoundry1-c1) pJ per DRAM byte in the DDR PHY, the I/O rail and the DRAM chips.
ml:dram:dram.e.unmetered.source: docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md rail-split table row 'DRAM, tensor load' and unmetered-fit table row 'per DRAM byte'; docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json unmetered.<card>.coef.dram_pj_per_byte; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'Rail split, DRAM read'

ml:dram:dram.e.vs-scp.statement: On random data DRAM is 30x the energy of the shire's own scratchpad per byte read (132.6 against 4.40 pJ/B) and 17x per byte written; relaying a result through DRAM costs 12.9-13.1x handing it to the next shire.
ml:dram:dram.e.vs-scp.source: docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md:37 ('DRAM is 30x the energy ...'), the random-data rows of its tables; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'The relay (V3)' (E29)
ml:dram:dram.e.vs-scp.page: Hand it to the next shire

ml:dram:dram.e.writeback.statement: Stores to DRAM through the L1 write-back path (fsw.ps) cost 341.5 pJ/B on random data at 27 GB/s: each store allocates its line, so the byte pays a DRAM read and a DRAM write.
ml:dram:dram.e.writeback.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['st_stream/dram/random']; docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table row 'fsw.ps stores to DRAM through the L1'

ml:dram:dram.lat.chase.statement: A DRAM pointer chase: 296.6-297.1 cycles from shires 0 and 31, 287.2-288.8 from shires 7 and 24 (479-495 ns at 600 MHz), in every pass on every card.
ml:dram:dram.lat.chase.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/lat.json items[LAT-M2].per_card.<card>.passes[].DRAM; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'L3 and DRAM latency by requesting shire' (E36)
ml:dram:dram.lat.chase.note: About 490 ns, a fifth more than an A100's HBM (405 ns).

ml:dram:dram.lat.clock-scaling.statement: At 800 MHz the chase reads 352-368 cycles (440-460 ns): the mesh and DDR parts do not scale with the minion clock; fitted, a DRAM load is 86.3 minion cycles + 344.8 ns.

ml:dram:dram.lat.dram-chip-share.statement: Of the 91-cycle constant (152 ns), about 28 cycles are the DRAM's own timing: the activate (tRCD, 11 cycles) and the read latency plus two 32-byte bursts (19.3 + 8.6 ns, 17 cycles). The rest, at most about 63 cycles (~105 ns), is the L3 home's miss path and its To_Sys crossings (about 12 cycles by the spec: an L3 miss is 42 shire clocks against 30 for a hit) plus the memory shire's port, clock crossing, controller and PHY.
ml:dram:dram.lat.dram-chip-share.source: anatomy page §4 ('Of the 91 cycles (152 ns), the DRAM chip itself accounts for about 28'); dram.ctl.tRCD, dram.ctl.RL-WL, dram.ctl.burst; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.11 Table 1 ('L3 cache read hit 30', 'L3 cache read miss 42 + NoC & Mem latency')
ml:dram:dram.lat.dram-chip-share.note: The 91 is a DRAM load minus an L3 hit at the same home (dram.lat.model), so it includes the home's extra work on a miss, not only the memory shire. 'At most' because each hop further out that the memory shires might sit moves 12 cycles from the constant into the mesh legs.

ml:dram:dram.lat.model.statement: Whole DRAM load = 110 + 12 x hops(requester -> L3 home) + 91 + 12 x hops(L3 home -> memory shire) cycles; left as fitted on aifoundry2, within +-3 cycles for 97.0% of lines on aifoundry2, 92.9% on aifoundry3, 94.4% on aifoundry1-c1.
ml:dram:dram.lat.model.source: anatomy page §4 (formula); docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM latency against the 19 September model' (E35, docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P2)
ml:dram:dram.lat.model.note: Refitted pass by pass the constant reads 90-91 on all three cards (docs/reports/data/2026-09-26-memprobe-3cards/cards.json ms_const).

ml:dram:dram.lat.ms-hops.statement: With the memory shires one hop outside the grid, the memory shire's position adds 12-84 cycles (1-7 hops from the L3 home, 2.6 on average).

ml:dram:dram.lat.ms-internal.statement: How the ~63 cycles beyond the DRAM's own timing split between the L3 home's miss handling and To_Sys crossings, the memory shire's NoC AXI port and clock crossing, the address strip, the controller's port, CAM and scheduler, the DFI and the PHY's transmit and receive paths is not known.
ml:dram:dram.lat.ms-internal.source: none: no memory-shire description is in the sources (hub ask 'ask-memshire', docs/reports/sources/limits-of-observability.data.json improvements[25])

ml:dram:dram.lat.typical.statement: A typical DRAM load, timed one at a time: 299 cycles (500 ns at 600 MHz), the median of 4,500 loads from shire 0 to random lines; 299 in each of 15 passes on three cards.
ml:dram:dram.lat.typical.source: docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html headline tile 'A DRAM load, typical' (19 Sep: 4,500 loads; 26 Sep: 15 passes on three cards)

ml:dram:dram.org.capacity.statement: 32 GB of LPDDR4X on the V3 cards (a Micron part): 2 GB, i.e. 16 Gbit, per channel; the chip supports up to 32 GB 'using LPDDR4X at 16 Gbits per channel'.
ml:dram:dram.org.capacity.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.1 ('32GB (Micron part) v3 card'); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1; external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:389-398 (MR8 density decode to 32 GB)

ml:dram:dram.org.die-internals.statement: The die's internal organisation below the bank (subarrays or mats, cells per bitline, open or folded bitlines, sense-amplifier variant, wordline boost and array voltages, cell capacitance, process node) is vendor-proprietary and appears in no ET source; the diagram's transistor level is therefore JEDEC/textbook GENERIC.
ml:dram:dram.org.die-internals.source: none (absence noted across external/et-man, external/core-et, external/et-platform)

ml:dram:dram.org.geometry.statement: Each channel is one rank of 8 banks x 131,072 rows x 2 KB pages (1,024 columns of 16 bits): 8 x 131,072 x 2 KB = 2 GB, matching the capacity. One activate therefore senses 16,384 bits into one bank's sense amplifiers.
ml:dram:dram.org.geometry.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4639-4654 (3 bank, 10 column, 17 row address bits); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:38 (`DDR_BANKS_SIZE 3`); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4539 (ODTMAP rank 0 only); JEDEC JESD209-4 addressing for a 16 Gb-per-channel LPDDR4 die (8 banks, R0-R16, C0-C9, 2 KB page)
ml:dram:dram.org.geometry.note: The geometry is what the programmed map and the capacity require and what JEDEC specifies for this density (GENERIC); the part's datasheet, which would confirm it, is not in the sources.

ml:dram:dram.org.line-vs-page.statement: A 64-byte line uses 512 of the 16,384 bits an activate senses: 1/32 of the open row. The other 31 lines of that row (8 KB apart in the address space) can then be read as row hits until the row closes.

ml:dram:dram.org.part.statement: The exact LPDDR4X part (Micron part number), its die density, the number of dies per package and whether each channel is one x16 die or two byte-mode dies are not in any source. The firmware reads the vendor (MR5; Micron = 0xFF) and density (MR8) at every boot and logs them, but no log has been captured.
ml:dram:dram.org.part.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.1; external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:364-398 (ddr_config: 'DRAM vendor = MICRON', 'DRAM size = 32GB'); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:936-1027 (ms_verify_ddr_density; comment 'for the micron part it is 0x10 for 32gb and 0x18 for 64gb')
ml:dram:dram.org.part.note: The firmware labels MR8 density code 6 '64gb/32GB' (mem_controller_utils.c:1000-1004); in JEDEC LPDDR4 terms code 6 is 32 Gb per die, 16 Gb per channel (GENERIC), which fits 2 GB per channel.

ml:dram:dram.pwr.droop.statement: The memory shires' own voltage monitors read the 0.8 V DDR rail at 767-768 mV at idle, and it droops 0.86-1.01 mV per watt of off-rail DRAM power (1 mV ~ 1.2 W of DRAM): a proxy DRAM meter, refreshed every service-processor pass.
ml:dram:dram.pwr.droop.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DDR rail droop per off-rail DRAM watt' (E30, E46); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md 'A droop meter for DRAM'; horace2-telemetry.jsonl die_mv.ddr

ml:dram:dram.pwr.rails.statement: Three card rails serve the memory path: VDD_DDR (the memory shires, 0.8 V set point, 875 mV in the card's power-tree figure), VDD_QLP (the LPDDR4X I/O VDDQ; 640 mV set point read on aifoundry2, 620 mV in the figure) and VDD_Q (1.1 V: the LPDDR4X's VDDQ/VDD2 core supply, as the figure labels it). None reports current.
ml:dram:dram.pwr.rails.source: docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52 (from the power-tree images, external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf pp.2-4); docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace2-telemetry.jsonl fields reg_mv.ddr = 800, reg_mv.vddqlp = 640, reg_mv.vddq = 1100
ml:dram:dram.pwr.rails.note: JEDEC LPDDR4X (GENERIC): VDD1 1.8 V, VDD2 1.1 V, VDDQ 0.6 V. Which card rail feeds the DRAM's VDD1 is not in the sources.

ml:dram:dram.seq.load.03.statement: The memory shire accepts the read, crosses from the mesh clock into its own domain, uses PA[9] to pick controller u0 or u1 (the channel) and strips PA[9:6] from the address.
ml:dram:dram.seq.load.03.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1.1.1; external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/ms_regs.h:160 (ms_mem_ctl reset); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:21-22; clock crossing: anatomy page §4 ('the crossings between the 933 MHz DDR clock and the mesh')
ml:dram:dram.seq.load.03.note: Where inside the memory shire the clock crossing sits, and whether its logic runs at 933 MHz, is inferred, not documented.

ml:dram:dram.seq.load.05.statement: The controller issues ACTIVATE (ACT-1, ACT-2) with bank and row; the PHY drives it onto the channel's CA pins at 1,866 MHz.

ml:dram:dram.seq.load.09.statement: After the read latency the DRAM drives two BL16 bursts, 32 bytes each, at 3,733 MT/s with read DBI; the PHY's trained receivers capture them on the strobe.

ml:dram:dram.seq.store.04.statement: The DRAM's write drivers overpower the selected sense amplifiers through the column-select transistors; the latches flip and, through the still-open access transistors, charge or discharge the cell capacitors.

ml:dram:dram.topo.controllers.statement: Each memory shire holds two Synopsys uMCTL2 DDR controller instances, one per 16-bit channel: the firmware programs controller blocks 0 and 1 of every memory shire, and the memory shire has separate mode-register read-back registers for 'memory controller 0' and 'memory controller 1'.
ml:dram:dram.topo.controllers.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.17 §1.5 ('connected to two memory controllers that each have a 16-bit LPPDR4X channel'); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.515 Table 15-90 (ddrc_u0_mrr_data, ddrc_u1_mrr_data); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:83-88 (get_ddrc_address: block 1 at +0x1000), :604-607 (ms_write_both_ddrc_reg); external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf pdf p.88 (errata 5.2 cites the uMCTL2 Databook v3.50a)
ml:dram:dram.topo.controllers.note: The datasheet disagrees: 'two 16-bit LPDDR4X physical interfaces sharing a single 32-bit controller' (external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7). Firmware and PRM agree on two controllers; see dram.topo.phy and the ask.

ml:dram:dram.topo.memshires.statement: Eight memory shires, four on the west side (0-3) and four on the east side (4-7) of the die, each driving two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels: 16 channels in all.
ml:dram:dram.topo.memshires.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.17 §1.5 (txt line 544-548); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7 and §7.1
ml:dram:dram.topo.memshires.note: West 0-3 / east 4-7 is the PRM's and the firmware's naming; the latency fit's logical map draws them above and below the grid (chip-diagram fact fw.memshires).

ml:dram:dram.topo.noc-port.statement: The NoC connects three ports to each memory shire (memory traffic, global-atomic responses, ESR accesses); the memory port is an AXI slave with a 512-bit data path (a whole 64-byte line per beat), and the NoC side delivers at most 32 GB/s per memory shire, almost twice the LPDDR4X side.
ml:dram:dram.topo.noc-port.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1.1 and §7.1.1.1

ml:dram:dram.topo.packages.statement: Four LPDDR4X packages on the card, each with four 16-bit channels (64 bits per package, 256 bits in all); two memory shires share each package.
ml:dram:dram.topo.packages.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.17 §1.5; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7 ('Two Memshires communicate with each 64-bit LPDDR4X memory device'); external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.3 ('4 x LPDDR4x DRAM devices for a combined 256-bit memory interface')
ml:dram:dram.topo.packages.note: The datasheet's §2.2.2 (pdf p.16) calls each package a 'bank' ('four banks of LPDDR4X memory. Each bank is controlled by two Memory Shires'): not a DRAM bank. The diagram should say 'package'.

ml:dram:dram.topo.phy.statement: One DDR PHY per memory shire serves both channels: the firmware writes one PHY training message block per memory shire, with the DRAM's MR14 (VREF-DQ) set for 'Channel A' and 'Channel B'; the open RTL gives the memory shire's DDR subsystem 4 data-byte lanes (DBYTEs, 2 per 16-bit channel), 6 address/command blocks (ANIBs) and a 16-bit DRAM data width.
ml:dram:dram.topo.phy.source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:190-192 (ms_patch_phy_ram_before_training); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:778-783 (ms_write_phy_ram: one PHY RAM window per memory shire); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:40 (DDR_DRAM_DATA_SIZE 16), :48-49 (DDR_NUM_ANIBS 6, DDR_NUM_DBYTES 4); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 (ddrc_reset_ctl 'DDRC PUB reset')
ml:dram:dram.topo.phy.note: The PHY stores up to four PSTATEs of training values (errata 5.4, pdf p.90) and has a PUB: a Synopsys DesignWare LPDDR4-class PHY, product and version not named in any source. core-et is the Erbium-branch open drop; its memory-shire headers match the ET-SoC-1 firmware wherever both speak (see dram.addr.*).

ml:dram:dram.topo.pll.statement: The boot firmware programs the memory PLL in memory shire 0 and memory shire 4 only: one PLL per side.
ml:dram:dram.topo.pll.note: How the clock reaches memory shires 1-3 and 5-7 is not described; presumably distributed along each side.

ml:dram:gen.cell.statement: A DRAM bit is one 1T1C cell: an NMOS access transistor whose gate is the wordline and whose drain is the bitline, in series with a storage capacitor; the stored charge is the bit, it leaks away (hence refresh), and reading it is destructive until the sense amplifier restores it.
ml:dram:gen.cell.source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM; no ET source describes the die)

ml:dram:gen.column.statement: Read: the column decoder raises a column-select line, turning on column-select NMOS pairs that connect the chosen sense amplifiers to local and then global I/O lines, where secondary sense amplifiers pick up the data; LPDDR4 fetches 16 bits per DQ per READ (16n prefetch), 256 bits for a x16 channel, and serialises them 16:1 onto each pin.
ml:dram:gen.column.source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 LPDDR4 16n prefetch; array circuit textbook)

ml:dram:gen.commands.statement: LPDDR4 commands travel on a 6-bit single-data-rate command/address bus: an ACTIVATE is two 2-clock parts (ACT-1, ACT-2), a READ or WRITE is RD-1/WR-1 plus CAS-2 (4 clocks), a PRECHARGE 2 clocks.

ml:dram:gen.equalize.statement: Between accesses each bitline pair is held at half the array voltage by a precharge/equalize circuit (typically three NMOS: two tie BL and /BL to the half-voltage, one shorts them together); the equalize signal turns off just before a wordline rises.

ml:dram:gen.io.statement: LPDDR4X signals use LVSTL: each DQ driver pulls up to a 0.6 V VDDQ or down to ground, and the receiver terminates to ground, so a driven 1 draws current through the termination and a 0 almost none; DBI inverts a byte that holds more than four ones. (LPDDR4's LVSTL pull-up is usually an NMOS, N-over-N; the transistor choice is the vendor's.)
ml:dram:gen.io.note: ET has read and write DBI on (dram.ctl.dbi); the card's VDD_QLP set point is 620-640 mV (dram.pwr.rails).

ml:dram:gen.jedec-match.statement: The programmed timings are close to JEDEC LPDDR4's limits for a 16 Gb-per-channel die at 3,733 MT/s, as recalled from JESD209-4 and not checked against the standard: tRCD and tRPpb 18 ns minimum, tRAS 42 ns, tRRD 10 ns, tFAW 40 ns, tRFCab 280 ns; RL 36 (with read DBI) and WL 16 are the fixed read and write latencies for this rate, and tREFI 3.875 us is just under the 3.904 us maximum interval.
ml:dram:gen.jedec-match.source: GENERIC comparison: JEDEC JESD209-4 values recalled, not checked against the standard (no ET source); ET values from dram.ctl.*
ml:dram:gen.jedec-match.note: tRFCab = 280 ns is the JEDEC value for 12-16 Gb per channel, a cross-check on the die density.

ml:dram:gen.refresh.statement: All-bank refresh: the die's internal counter supplies the row addresses and each REFab activates and precharges a batch of rows in every bank at once; JEDEC LPDDR4 asks for 8,192 refresh commands per 32 ms retention window at normal temperature, which with 131,072 rows per bank means 16 rows of each bank per REFab.
ml:dram:gen.refresh.source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 tREFW 32 ms, 8,192 REF); rows per bank from dram.org.geometry
ml:dram:gen.refresh.note: ET's tREFI 3.875 us is slightly shorter than JEDEC's 3.904 us, so 8,192 refreshes take 31.7 ms.

ml:dram:gen.sense.statement: Each cell shares its charge with its bitline, nudging it slightly above or below the half-voltage; the bitline sense amplifier, a cross-coupled latch of two NMOS and two PMOS, is then fired (NMOS side pulled to ground, PMOS side to the array voltage) and drives the pair to full rail, which also rewrites the cell. The row of latched sense amplifiers is the open page ('row buffer').
ml:dram:gen.sense.note: On the ET-SoC-1's channels one activate latches 16,384 bits (dram.org.geometry).

ml:dram:gen.wordline.statement: Activate: the row address is decoded, and the selected (sub-)wordline driver pulls its wordline up to a boosted voltage above the array voltage, so every access NMOS on that row turns fully on and passes a full level.

ml:l1:g.compare.statement: A tag comparator is one XNOR per bit (about 8-12 transistors) and an AND tree over the 33 bits; four run on every access, hit or miss.
ml:l1:g.compare.source: textbook logic (GENERIC); four comparators and 33-bit tags from l1.phased, l1.metadata

ml:l1:g.flipflop.statement: The valid and LRU bits are edge-triggered flip-flops: two latches in master-slave, about 20-24 transistors each.

ml:l1:g.latch-cell.statement: A static CMOS D-latch (transmission-gate or clocked-inverter type) stores a bit on a pair of cross-coupled inverters with a clocked feedback path: about 8-12 transistors per bit, full-swing, no precharge, no sense amplifier, readable without disturbing the stored value.

ml:l1:g.latch-read.statement: A latch-array read is logic: the registered address drives a decoder or a mux tree (128:1 per output bit, e.g. seven 2:1 levels or four 4:1 levels), and only the nodes whose value changes spend energy, so read energy depends on the data.

ml:l1:g.latch-write.statement: A latch-array write: the write-address decoder enables one row's integrated clock gate (a latch plus an AND, about 10-16 transistors); its gated clock goes high and every latch in that row becomes transparent and takes the write bus, which an opposite-phase latch holds steady for the whole phase.
ml:l1:g.latch-write.source: textbook latch register-file design (GENERIC); the opposite-phase write latch and per-row gates are the ET pattern in l1.latch-rf

ml:l1:g.sram-6t.statement: For contrast, a 6T SRAM cell: two cross-coupled inverters (4 transistors) and two NMOS access transistors on complementary bitlines. A read precharges the bitlines, the wordline driver raises one wordline, one bitline droops by a fraction of VDD and a sense amplifier resolves it through a column mux; the cell needs a minimum voltage for read stability and writability, which is why SRAM usually gets its own higher rail.

ml:l1:l1.bank-enables.statement: Only the blocks a load needs are read: a scalar load enables the one block whose addr[4:3] matches (both of its 32-bit halves); a 32-byte packed-single (PS) vector load enables all four; a misaligned access also reads the next row in the following blocks.
ml:l1:l1.bank-enables.source: external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2123-2147; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.10 (text L352-361, worked examples)
ml:l1:l1.bank-enables.note: A 4-byte flw still reads the whole 64-bit block row: valid_h = valid_l (dcache_top.v:2141; the RTL comment at :2459 reads "OPTIMIZE, check if it can be split").

ml:l1:l1.bits.statement: Storage per minion: 32,768 data bits in latch RAM, 2,240 tag and state bits in latch register files, 64 valid and 256 LRU flip-flops. Over 1,088 minions that is 35.7 Mbit (4.25 MB) of latch-RAM data.

ml:l1:l1.bw.statement: L1 bandwidth: 14.5 TB/s over the chip with 32-byte vector loads on both harts (23.6 B per minion-cycle of the 32 designed); 6.2 TB/s in the memory-hierarchy probe's loop.

ml:l1:l1.e-fill.statement: Filling one 64-byte line from the own scratchpad into the L1: 238 pJ on random data (aifoundry2 221, aifoundry3 223, aifoundry1-c1 271), 101 pJ on zeros; random data adds 269 fJ per bit on the path into the L1.
ml:l1:l1.e-fill.note: Difference of two measured stride rows, times 2.

ml:l1:l1.e-scalar.statement: Scalar 4-byte accesses that hit the L1 (512 B table per hart, all 1,024 minions): flw 14.0 pJ [13.4-14.5], fsw 25.5 pJ [24.8-26.4]; the 8-lane gather fgw.ps 12.8 pJ and scatter fscw.ps 14.7 pJ per element.

ml:l1:l1.e-store-ratio.statement: A store costs more than a load of the same size: 1.82x for scalar (25.5 / 14.0 pJ), 1.33x for 32-byte vectors (0.72 / 0.54 pJ/B), consistent with the store touching the array twice (S2 read, S4 write).

ml:l1:l1.e-vload.statement: One 32-byte vector load (flw.ps) that hits the L1: 0.54 pJ/B on random data [0.52-0.56] = 17.3 pJ per load (aifoundry2 17.6, aifoundry3 17.3, aifoundry1-c1 16.6); 0.39 pJ/B on zeros = 12.5 pJ per load. Above idle, including the instruction.

ml:l1:l1.e-vstore.statement: One 32-byte vector store (fsw.ps) that hits the L1: 0.72 pJ/B on random data [0.66-0.81] = 23.0 pJ per store (aifoundry2 23.4, aifoundry3 23.0, aifoundry1-c1 22.7); 0.41 pJ/B on zeros = 13.1 pJ.

ml:l1:l1.firmware-mode.statement: The firmware sets D1Split and ScpEnable before every launch, so a kernel runs with 512 B of L1 cache per hart (2 sets x 4 ways x 64 B) and a 3 KB scratchpad.

ml:l1:l1.icache-sram.statement: Contrast at the same level: the neighbourhood's instruction-cache data RAM (mbi) is 'saduls0g4l1p512x144m4b1...', the same 1PUHD macro family as the shire cache's data panels, which the spec calls 'SRAM memory panels'; the PRM calls the SADULS family SRAMs, and the neighbourhood document says its memory cells must sit in an HV region. Its bitcell is as unknown as the shire cache's.
ml:l1:l1.icache-sram.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.51 Table 14 (icache_ram (mbi)), pdf p.48 §2.14.5; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.346 ('Configuration bits for SADULS SRAM's'); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf pdf p.14 §4.2
ml:l1:l1.icache-sram.note: external/core-et/rtl/libs/macros/icache_data_ram.v calls it a '512 x 144-bit synchronous SRAM', but that file is a behavioural stand-in (Ainekko, 2026), like the L1's dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram.v, and says nothing about the cell.

ml:l1:l1.icg-cells.statement: The clock gates of the latch arrays are standard cells when the ASIC cell switch is on: HDBULT08_CKGTPLT_V7Y2_2 (rising-edge gate, per row) and HDBULT08_CKGTNLT_V5Y2_2 (falling-edge gate, write-data latch). Other cells named in the RTL come from HDBULT08_* and HDBULT11_* families.
ml:l1:l1.icg-cells.source: external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/et_clk_gate.v:14-18; external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/et_clk_gate_n.v:14-18; external/core-et/rtl/inc/libs_defines.vh:8-9 (switch off in the open release: "Standard cells not available")
ml:l1:l1.icg-cells.note: Library vendor, track height and threshold flavour are not stated (l1.u-library).

ml:l1:l1.knee.statement: The measured knee confirms 512 B per hart: hart 1 reads 5.25 cycles at 256 B, 5.256 at 512 B and 39.0 at 768 B (a miss to the L2 read buffer), in every pass on three cards.

ml:l1:l1.latch-rf.statement: The ET latch register-file library ("Latch based Register Files with registered read output") shows the write and read mechanism these arrays use: write data is captured by a low-phase latch clocked by a negative clock gate one phase before the write; the decoded write address enables one per-row clock gate; that row's latches are transparent while its gated clock is high; the read address is registered on the rising edge and the read is a combinational select rf[rd_addr_reg] (no bitline, no sense amplifier in the model).
ml:l1:l1.latch-rf.source: external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/rf_latch_1r_1w_reg.v:4-52 (timing diagram and notes), 88-96 (write-data latch), 101-136 (per-row clock gates and latches), 139-149 (registered read address, combinational read)
ml:l1:l1.latch-rf.note: core-et-main maps the D-cache LRAM wrappers to exactly this contract, "preview-plus-registered-read RF" (external/core-et-main/docs/latch_translation.md:55-56, 93-96; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/minion/dcache/rtl/minion_dcache_128x64_1r1w_lram.sv:35-63). Whether the silicon macro is this library cell-for-cell is unknown (l1.u-cell).

ml:l1:l1.latency.statement: L1 hit: 5.25 cycles load-to-use in a dependent pointer chase (8.75 ns at 600 MHz), per-pass ranges 5.247-5.259, in every pass on three cards.

ml:l1:l1.latency-5.statement: A dependent L1 load issues 5 cycles after the previous one: ID, EX, TAG, MEM, WB (data leaves S3 at WB) and the next ID. The 0.25 cycle in 5.25 fits 2 cycles of loop overhead per 8 unrolled loads; the anatomy page sets an L1 hit to 5 cycles.
ml:l1:l1.latency-5.source: external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.9 (text L201-208), pdf p.12 (text L234-235: "DCache data is available at the WB stage or later"); workloads/memhier/kernel/memhier.c:36-44; workloads/memprobe/README.md ("offset chosen so an L1 hit reads the 5 cycles")
ml:l1:l1.latency-5.note: Stage-by-stage timing is inferred from the documents; no probe times a single stage (l1.u-cycles).

ml:l1:l1.lram.statement: The data array is not SRAM: it is built from latch RAM, "4 LRAM (Latch-RAM) blocks of 128 rows and 64 bits per row", each block with a single read port and a single write port.
ml:l1:l1.lram.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29 (§3.2, text L1269-1271) and glossary pdf p.61 ("LRAM Latch Random Access Memory"); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.9 (§2.1.1.5, text L346)
ml:l1:l1.lram.note: Answers the lab lead's "not SRAM" for the L1: latch RAM. Both the design doc and the public datasheet say so.

ml:l1:l1.lram-addr.statement: LRAM row address = {set[3:0], half-line bit, way[1:0]} = {addr[9:5], way[1:0]}: 7 bits, 128 rows. Address bits [4:3] choose the block (8 bytes each); one row across the 4 blocks is 32 bytes, half a line; a 64-byte line occupies 2 rows, and the 4 ways of a half-line sit in 4 adjacent rows.
ml:l1:l1.lram-addr.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29-30 (§3.2, text L1276-1296, Figure 10); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.10 (Figure 2-3); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_data_array.v:46-50

ml:l1:l1.lram-macros.statement: In the RTL each 128 x 64 block is a wrapper of two 128 x 32 one-read-one-write LRAM macros (low and high 32-bit halves) with their own read and write enables: 8 macros (dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram) per minion.

ml:l1:l1.lram-model.statement: The released LRAM macro is only a behavioural model ("One-read, one-write register file ... synchronous write, synchronous read"); the cell-level design of the silicon macro is not in the open release.
ml:l1:l1.lram-model.note: See unknown l1.u-cell. The port list (clk, rd/wr enable, 7-bit rd/wr address, 32-bit data) is all the model fixes.

ml:l1:l1.lru.statement: Replacement is LRU: 16 bits per set (a 4 x 4 order matrix), in flip-flops, updated in S2 on every cacheable access; hard- and soft-locked ways are excluded when choosing the victim.
ml:l1:l1.lru.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:31; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_lru_array.v (RST_EN_FF per set); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2722-2744, 3150-3159; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.25 (text L954)

ml:l1:l1.lv-region.statement: The eight minions of a neighbourhood sit in its low-voltage (LV) region with their own clock; the neighbourhood says the memory cells of its ICache data RAMs "need to be placed in an HV region", so those RAMs were moved out into the shire channel.
ml:l1:l1.lv-region.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.6 (§2, text L108-112), pdf p.7 (§2.2, text L150-154), pdf p.14 (§4.2, text L511-518)

ml:l1:l1.metadata.statement: Metadata: 64 entries (16 sets x 4 ways) of tag PA[39:7] (33 bits) + 2-bit line state = 35 bits, held in four latch register files (one per way, 16 entries, read in the same cycle); the 64 valid bits are flip-flops.
ml:l1:l1.metadata.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.31 (§3.3, text L1350-1361) and pdf p.57 (§3.12.1, text L2457-2458); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_metadata_array.v:39-65 (rf_latch_1r_1w per way, valid in RST_EN_FF); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_types.vh:183-187; external/core-et/rtl/libs/rf_latches/rf_latch_1r_1w.v:49-50 ("read latency = 0")

ml:l1:l1.mh.statement: Two miss handlers per minion (DCACHE_MH_FILE_SIZE = 2, the only verified value): at most two outstanding cacheable line misses; a later access to a line already being filled joins the same handler.
ml:l1:l1.mh.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.34-35 (§3.6, text L1449-1480); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:79

ml:l1:l1.miss-l2.statement: When the load misses the L1: 36 cycles if the line is in the L2 read buffer, 47 if it is in the L2 or the own scratchpad; hart 1 pays 3 more (39 and 50).
ml:l1:l1.miss-l2.note: The L1's own share of these cycles (miss detection, miss handler, fill write, replay) is not measured apart.

ml:l1:l1.modes.statement: Three modes (mcache_control D1Split, ScpEnable): shared (both harts, all 16 sets); split (hart 0 sets 0-7, hart 1 sets 14-15, sets 8-13 unused); scratchpad (hart 0 sets 12-13, hart 1 sets 14-15, sets 0-11 = 48 lines = 3 KB of tensor scratchpad, hart 0 only).
ml:l1:l1.modes.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.245-246 (§8.3.1, Table 8.4, text L5977-6010); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:130 (DCACHE_TL_SCP_MAX_IDX 48)
ml:l1:l1.modes.note: The Minion Overview slide draws split mode as 2 KB per hart; the PRM table is followed here.

ml:l1:l1.phased.statement: Tag first, then data: in S1 the physical tag is compared with all 4 ways (four comparators) and the hit way is encoded; the S2 data read then reads only that way's row, because the way is part of the LRAM row address.
ml:l1:l1.phased.source: external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_top.v:2108-2121 ("CAM for the tags"), 2145; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_data_array.v:49-50; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.24-25 (§3.1.2-3.1.3)
ml:l1:l1.phased.note: GENERIC: a serial tag-then-data cache reads one way instead of four, at the cost of a pipeline stage.

ml:l1:l1.pipeline.statement: Six DCache stages, locked to the integer pipeline: pre-S0 = ID (arbitration bids), S0 = EX (address, grant), S1 = TAG (TLB, metadata read, tag match, PMA, data-array address), S2 = MEM (data-array read, hit/miss, replay queue, miss handler), S3 = WB (align, sign-extend, return to core or VPU), S4 (data-array write port), S5 (store data bypass to S3).
ml:l1:l1.pipeline.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.22 (Figure 3), pdf p.23-28 (§3.1.1-3.1.6); external/core-et/docs/FE-Intpipe-Description.pdf, pdf p.9 (§3.1, text L201-212), pdf p.12 (text L224-227)

ml:l1:l1.rail.statement: The L1 is powered from the minion rail (VDD_MNN), not the SRAM rail (VDD_SRAM, the shire-cache arrays): an L1-hit loop puts 83% of its power over idle on the minion rail and 2% on the SRAM rail; on 19 September an 8-byte ld L1 hit cost 40.7 pJ on the minion rail and 1.3 pJ on the SRAM rail.
ml:l1:l1.rail.source: docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md:168; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/power/summary.json: summary.l1.pj_per_load (minion 40.74, sram 1.33, noc 0.56, board 56.47); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:14, 44, 46

ml:l1:l1.rq.statement: Replay queue of 8 entries, pre-allocated at ID; a missing or rejected instruction waits there and re-enters the pipeline; when it is full the core is told id_core_ready = 0.
ml:l1:l1.rq.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.38 (§3.7, text L1634-1649); external/core-et/rtl/inc/minion_defines.vh:151

ml:l1:l1.s0-arb.statement: Pre-S0 priority, high to low: cache-ops metadata read, debug, write-back unit (reads the data array), replay queue, cache-ops L1 prefetch, core intpipe. The VPU scratchpad read, Reduce, TensorLoad and cache-op prefetch can also take S0.
ml:l1:l1.s0-arb.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.24 (§3.1.1, text L839-857)

ml:l1:l1.s4-arb.statement: One write port per block, static priority: stores in S4, fills from the SEND port, L2 fills from the miss handlers, TensorLoad transformation writes, configuration clear, cache-ops clear, debug. A fill may write only if there is no store and the read port was not granted in the previous cycle.
ml:l1:l1.s4-arb.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.27 (§3.1.5, text L1116-1129)

ml:l1:l1.scp-impl.statement: Scratchpad mode is implemented in the same array: two more tag bits are kept and the two set MSBs are forced to 11, so the cache uses only sets 12-15; changing ScpEnable drains the pipeline, writes zeros into every line of sets 0-13 and invalidates their metadata.
ml:l1:l1.scp-impl.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.30-31 (§3.2.1, text L1318-1347); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.246 (text L6012-6019); external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/dcache/dcache_metadata_array.v:92-108 (cfg_clear_low)

ml:l1:l1.size.statement: Each minion has a private 4 KB L1 data cache: 16 sets x 4 ways x 64-byte lines (set = PA[9:6]).
ml:l1:l1.size.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.9 (§2.1.1.5, text L341-345); external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29 (§3.2, text L1266); external/core-et/rtl/inc/minion_defines.vh:125,143 (DCACHE_SETS 16, DCACHE_WAYS 4); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:27 (line 64 B)

ml:l1:l1.tensorload.statement: TensorLoad (unit TL0) writes L2 responses straight into scratchpad rows through the write port; TensorLoadB (TL1) skips the array and fills a 4-entry VPU buffer under 4 (up to 6) credits; up to 4 L2 transfers are in flight; transposes and interleaves stage through a 128-byte buffer and write the LRAM in 8-byte chunks.
ml:l1:l1.tensorload.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.3.4), pdf p.40-43 (§3.9.1-3.9.2); external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:108

ml:l1:l1.tl-latency.statement: One minion's TensorLoad into its L1 scratchpad: 16 lines (1 KB) take 160.4 cycles from the L2 and 160.1 from the own scratchpad; 8 lines 80.1; 4 lines 41.9 cycles; the same on three cards.

ml:l1:l1.tl-rate.statement: About 10 cycles per 64-byte line into the scratchpad (6.4 B per cycle): what 4 transfers in flight over a round trip of about 40 cycles allow.
ml:l1:l1.tl-rate.source: derived from docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/lat.json LAT-S2 (160.4 / 80.1 / 41.9 cycles for 16 / 8 / 4 lines) and external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:108
ml:l1:l1.tl-rate.note: Little's law with the RTL constant; the round trip itself is not separately measured.

ml:l1:l1.tlb.statement: An 8-entry TLB (a latch register file) translates in S1 (4 KB, 2 MB and 1 GB pages); the neighbourhood document notes that "Virtual Memory logic is unused in A0".
ml:l1:l1.tlb.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/dcache_defines.vh:105; external/core-et/rtl/shire/minion/tlb_top.v:277-285; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.4.1); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.6 (footnote 1, text L143)
ml:l1:l1.tlb.note: workloads/memprobe/README.md treats kernel addresses as physical ("offset bits are physical address bits").

ml:l1:l1.transistors.statement: Estimate: at 8-12 transistors per latch bit, the data array holds about 0.26-0.39 million storage transistors per minion (0.29-0.43 billion on the chip, 1.2-1.8% of its >24 billion), against 0.2 million for the same 4 KB in 6T SRAM.
ml:l1:l1.transistors.source: l1.bits x GENERIC transistors per bit; chip total from docs/findings/01-resources.md:101
ml:l1:l1.transistors.note: GENERIC count per bit; the real latch cell is unknown (l1.u-cell). Excludes decoders, clock gates and read muxes.

ml:l1:l1.u-cell.statement: What is inside the dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram macro on silicon: standard-cell latches placed like the rf_latch_1r_1w_reg library, or a custom or compiled latch-array macro? Which latch cell (transistors per bit), and is the read a static mux tree or a precharged read bitline with a keeper or sense stage?
ml:l1:l1.u-cell.note: Settles: the transistor-level panel of the L1 diagram, now drawn from the generic latch-RF template (l1.latch-rf, g.latch-cell, g.latch-read): cell topology, read path, and the transistor estimate l1.transistors.

ml:l1:l1.voltage.statement: The latch arrays switch at the minion-rail voltage: 0.517 V at 600 MHz (0.568 V at 700, 0.618 V at 800). The card's power tree gives the minion rail 400 mV nominal, and the firmware limits it to 400-620 mV.

ml:l1:l1.vpu-port.statement: The array feeds one 256-bit register-file entry of all 8 VPU lanes per cycle (DCACHE_DATA_SIZE 256).

ml:l1:l1.vpu-scp-read.statement: The VPU reads the scratchpad directly: its request in S1 pre-empts any other S1 operation (sent to the replay queue), no tag check is made, and the 256 bits are delivered in S3, two cycles later (one extra register stage for timing).
ml:l1:l1.vpu-scp-read.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.12-13 (§2.3, §2.3.1, text L416-451, Figure 1)

ml:l1:l1.why-latch.statement: Why latches: the data cache sits inside the minion, in the neighbourhood's LV region. The neighbourhood document says that "the memory cells used to implement the ICache data RAMs need to be placed in an HV region"; that the same holds for the shire cache's SRAM panels, and that the data cache is a latch array because latches are ordinary logic that runs on the minion supply, is our inference.
ml:l1:l1.why-latch.source: combines l1.lram (external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf pdf p.29) and l1.lv-region (external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf pdf p.14 §4.2); minion-rail limits docs/research/power-telemetry.md:189-190 (bl2_pmic_controller.h:165-244); Vmin external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.51 Tables 13-14
ml:l1:l1.why-latch.note: The documents never state this rationale for the data cache (asked). A voltage argument is consistent with it but does not prove it, and it is about the listed Vmin of these macros only: the firmware limits the minion rail to 400-620 mV (400 mV nominal), while the 1PUHD data panels list 585 mV as their lowest Vmin (RM0) and the 2PUHDRF tag-state RAM 540 mV (Shire Cache Specification pdf p.51 Tables 13-14).

ml:l2:l2.atomic.statement: Each bank has an atomic unit (32-, 64- and 256-bit operands: swap, add, and, or, xor, min/max signed and unsigned, float min/max). An atomic keeps its sub-bank busy from the read through the operation to the write.

ml:l2:l2.bank-select.statement: L2 and scratchpad requests go to the bank chosen by PA[7:6], so consecutive 64 B lines rotate through banks 0-3.

ml:l2:l2.banks.statement: The shire cache is four identical banks; each bank is an independent L2 cache with its own request queue, pipeline and next-level ports. A bank takes at most one request per cycle and returns at most one 512-bit line per cycle.

ml:l2:l2.bits.statement: Bits stored per shire, ECC included: data 64 x 4,096 x 144 = 37,748,736; tag 16 x 1,024 x 116 = 1,900,544; tag state 16 x 1,024 x 40 = 655,360; 40,304,640 in all (about 40.3 Mbit, of which 33.6 Mbit is the 4 MB of data).
ml:l2:l2.bits.source: derived from the macro sizes, external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.51

ml:l2:l2.bw.measured.statement: With 1 KB tensor loads on every minion the L2 delivers 2.45 TB/s chip-wide: 4.0 B per minion-cycle = 128 B per shire-cycle, half the four banks' 256 B per shire-cycle. The own scratchpad gives the same (2.46 TB/s).

ml:l2:l2.cbuf.statement: Each bank has a 32-entry coalescing buffer that merges write-arounds (TensorStores to L3 or a remote scratchpad) in the L2. It flushes a line once all four 128-bit quadwords are written, or on an explicit flush.

ml:l2:l2.clock-gating.statement: Module-level clock gaters (esr_sc_clk_gate_disable) stop the bank's clock when it has no outstanding requests (errata RTLMIN-6235, which is why the bank's cycle counter under-counts). The reimplementation gates each RAM's clock on only for the ram_delay cycles of an access.
ml:l2:l2.clock-gating.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.97 §4.1; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf, pdf p.82 §4.3; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/shirecache/rtl/shirecache_pipe_data_ram_wrap.sv:1-7, 46-66
ml:l2:l2.clock-gating.note: The per-access RAM clock enable is from the Ainekko reimplementation, not the ET-SoC-1 RTL.

ml:l2:l2.data-ram.statement: Data RAM: each sub-bank is four 144-bit-wide panels, each holding one 128-bit quadword + 16 ECC bits (8 per 64 bits). A 64 B line is one row across the four panels (576 bits); a sub-bank's data RAM is 4,096 rows addressed by {way, set}.

ml:l2:l2.dataq.statement: The dataq holds one 64 B line per reqq entry in a two-ported register file (one write and one read port, each shared by 5 sources). BIST sees it as logical RAM mbq (64 x 4 x 144 bits, 1-cycle access) plus mbb (64 x 72 bits). Read hits normally bypass it straight to the response mux.
ml:l2:l2.dataq.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.35, pdf p.38-40 §2.7, pdf p.49; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:350-380

ml:l2:l2.decode.statement: L2 address fields: offset PA[5:0], bank PA[7:6], sub-bank PA[9:8], set from PA[10] (PA[19:10] for a full 4 MB L2; PA[16:10] with Mode 0's 7-bit set mask), tag above. The tag RAM stores 23 tag bits, which 'allows for down to 512k L2 allocation'.

ml:l2:l2.e.level.statement: Reading the L2 with 1 KB tensor loads on every minion at 600 MHz costs 3.11 pJ/B [1.42-4.99] above idle (per card: aifoundry2 2.64, aifoundry3 2.83, aifoundry1-c1 3.86). That is about 199 pJ per 64 B line for the whole path.
ml:l2:l2.e.level.note: The buffer's contents were not set; the scratchpad rows below control the data.

ml:l2:l2.e.rails.statement: No L2 hit has been split between the rails on three cards. Read as the shire's own scratchpad (1 KB tensor loads, no tag check, random data), the same arrays put 69, 68 and 49% of the power above idle on the SRAM rail, 24, 23 and 21% on the minion rail, 1% or less on the mesh and 7, 9 and 29% on no metered rail (aifoundry2, aifoundry3 and aifoundry1 card 1; the energy manual's catalogue, 26 September).
ml:l2:l2.e.rails.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.cards.<card>.summary['tload/scp/random'] (rails_over_w, over_idle_w), as Anatomy of a memory access §6 splits it (workloads/memprobe/build_report.py)
ml:l2:l2.e.rails.note: Until 28 September this row gave the first measurement, on 19 September on aifoundry2 alone (an L2 hit by 8-byte loads; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json power.l2); Anatomy of a memory access keeps those runs as one note, and its §6 shows this split. The unmetered share is highest on the card whose unmetered power rises most with its SRAM rail's (the energy manual's fit of the unmetered power, §4.5: unmetered.<card>.coef.sram).

ml:l2:l2.e.scalar.statement: One random flw from the L2 (a line per load) costs 336 pJ [315-369] at 27.5 G/s. One fsw costs 774 pJ: the store allocates the line and writes it back.

ml:l2:l2.e.tload-tstore.statement: Tensor load from the own scratchpad: 2.12 (zeros) / 4.43 (random) pJ/B. Tensor store into it: 4.65 / 8.58 pJ/B. A scratchpad write costs about twice a read.

ml:l2:l2.ecc.statement: All shire-cache RAMs have SECDED ECC (single-error correct, double-error detect): 6 bits per tag, 7 per tag-state row and 8 per 64 data bits, checked in stages te and de. On this chip ECC covers only the L2/L3/scratchpad SRAM and the instruction cache. Background ECC scrubbing is a reserved bit, 'implemented in Gepardo', a later chip.
ml:l2:l2.ecc.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.9, pdf p.48-49 §2.14.6.2, pdf p.99; docs/findings/15-earlier-findings.md:65-66

ml:l2:l2.freq.statement: The firmware reports the L2/SRAM frequency as equal to the minion frequency: 600 MHz at the governor's operating point used for every measurement here.

ml:l2:l2.lat.measured.statement: Load-to-use latency by pointer chase at 600 MHz: read-buffer hit 36.00 cycles (60 ns) and L2 or own-scratchpad hit 47.00 cycles (78 ns) on hart 0; hart 1 pays 3 more (39.0 and 50.0). Every pass on every card fell within 35.998-36.006 and 46.998-47.024.

ml:l2:l2.lat.overhead.statement: Measured minus spec is 26 cycles for both (47 - 21 = 36 - 10), so the path outside the shire cache is a constant and the 11-cycle read-buffer saving is all inside the bank. That is consistent with one shire clock being one minion cycle (l2.clock). Of the 26, the neighbourhood's request and response datapaths take at least 6 + 6, leaving about 14 for the minion's L1 miss detection, miss handler and fill-to-use.
ml:l2:l2.lat.overhead.source: derived from external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.11 Table 1, docs/findings/05-claims.md:421 and external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.20-21

ml:l2:l2.lat.spec.statement: Idle-cache latencies in shire clocks, from the neighbourhood's ET-Link request to its response, crossbars included: L2 hit 21, read-buffer hit 10, L2 miss 34 + NoC and L3/memory latency.

ml:l2:l2.leak.statement: SRAM-rail power at idle: 2.00 W for the chip (about 16 mW per MB if split evenly over the 128 MB of L2, L3 and scratchpad, the energy manual's denominator); 1.70 W at 67 C and 2.73 W at 82 C on aifoundry2; 0.051-0.066 W per degree C on the other cards.
ml:l2:l2.leak.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:184, 473; docs/findings/16-dvfs-and-leakage.md:141; docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md:110 ('Measured: 1.70 W at 67 °C') and its table (67 °C 1.698 W, 82 °C 2.726 W)
ml:l2:l2.leak.note: The per-MB split assumes the rail feeds the 128 MB evenly; what else is on the rail is unknown (asked).

ml:l2:l2.macro.count.statement: Per shire there are 64 data macros (4 banks x 4 sub-banks x 4 panels), 16 tag macros and 16 tag-state macros.
ml:l2:l2.macro.count.source: derived from external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.48 §2.14.5, p.47 §2.14.2-3 and p.51

ml:l2:l2.macro.data.statement: The data panel is the compiled macro 'saduls0g4l1p4096x144m4b4w0c0p0d0s1rm0sdrw11', RAM type 1PUHD: 4,096 words x 144 bits.
ml:l2:l2.macro.data.note: The spec gives the type code, not its meaning. Reading 1PUHD as single-port ultra-high-density follows common memory-compiler naming (GENERIC); no source states it.

ml:l2:l2.macro.name-decode.statement: Reading 'm4' and 'b4' in the data macro's name as a memory compiler's column-mux 4 and internal-bank 4 fields would make each 4096x144 panel about 1,024 wordlines by 576 bitline pairs, split into 4 banks, with each output bit chosen from 4 columns. No source defines the fields.
ml:l2:l2.macro.name-decode.note: This is naming-convention inference. The macro datasheet settles it.

ml:l2:l2.macro.state.statement: The tag-state RAM is 'saculs0g4l2p1024x40m4b1w0c0p0d0s1rm0rw11', RAM type 2PUHDRF: 1,024 words x 40 bits. The spec says the state RAM is two-ported (a read and a write per request).
ml:l2:l2.macro.state.note: Reading 'RF' in 2PUHDRF as register file follows common memory-compiler naming (GENERIC); no source states it.

ml:l2:l2.macro.tag.statement: The tag RAM is 'saduls0g4l1p1024x116m4b1w0c0p0d0s1rm0sdrw11', type 1PUHD: 1,024 words x 116 bits.

ml:l2:l2.macro.vendor.statement: The tag-state, tag and data panels are 'IP acquired from a third party vendor'. They are tested with a shared-bus BIST 'such as the Synopsys SMS (STAR Memory System)'. The BIST's logical RAMs per bank are mbs (tag state), mbt (tag), mbd (data), mbq (dataq) and mbi (instruction cache, bank 0 only).
ml:l2:l2.macro.vendor.note: The vendor and bitcell are not named. The Synopsys BIST and the name pattern point to a Synopsys-compiled memory, but that is an inference.

ml:l2:l2.nbr.response.statement: Back in the neighbourhood a response goes through the VC FIFO (min 2 cycles), the Fill FIFO (a 4-entry buffer drained out of order by an LRU 4:1 arbiter, min 2 cycles) and the minion's Fill FF, which splits 512 bits into two 256-bit beats (min 2 cycles): 6 cycles minimum for a minion.

ml:l2:l2.panel-select.statement: Only the panels holding the addressed quadwords are enabled (a 3-quadword partial write activates 3 panels), and the RAM inputs, address bits included, are held unchanged in cycles with no access, to save power.

ml:l2:l2.partition.default.statement: Firmware default partition (Mode 0): 2.5 MB scratchpad, 0.5 MB L2, 1 MB L3 per shire (80 / 16 / 32 MB for the chip). The service processor reads the sizes from the card's flash configuration and writes them to every bank; the chip comes out of reset in M0.
ml:l2:l2.partition.default.source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/minion_configuration.c:613-624; .../driver/bl2_cache_control.c:650-751; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.21-22 Table 6 and 'The chip will come out of reset in mode M0'; docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-cards/driver_config.json (l2_kb 16384, l3_kb 32768, scp_kb 81920 on every card)
ml:l2:l2.partition.default.note: Every lab card's driver reports M0's sizes (docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-cards/driver_config.json). Latency plateaus up to 64 KB do not test the 512 KB edge.

ml:l2:l2.partition.rows.statement: In Mode 0 the L2 occupies sets 0x280-0x2FF (128 of the 1,024 physical sets) of every sub-bank, set mask 0x7F: 4 banks x 4 sub-banks x 128 sets x 4 ways x 64 B = 512 KB. The scratchpad sits in sets 0x000-0x27F and the L3 in 0x300-0x3FF of the same RAMs.
ml:l2:l2.partition.rows.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.22 Table 7 (Mode 0 rows); pdf p.25 §1.4.1.4 (physical set = region set + set_base)
ml:l2:l2.partition.rows.note: So an L2 access lights only rows 640-767 of each tag/tag-state RAM and the matching {way,set} rows of the data RAMs; the other rows belong to scratchpad and L3.

ml:l2:l2.path.miss.statement: An L1 miss starts one of the minion's two miss handlers, which asks the L2 for the line. Loads leave on the miss interface (3 valid/ready pairs: regular, TensorLoad 0, TensorLoad 1). Stores, evicts, atomics and messages leave on the 256-bit evict interface.
ml:l2:l2.path.miss.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.15 Table 2; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.34-36 §3.6; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:448

ml:l2:l2.path.nbr-request.statement: Inside the neighbourhood a request passes the minion's Miss/Evict flip-flops, a 2:1 minion arbiter (evicts first), a flop, a two-stage 13:1 round-robin arbiter, a 1-cycle pre-processing stage and then one of five output FIFOs (four banks + UC, 3 entries each, with a 2-entry intermediate FIFO). Minimum latency for a minion's request is 6 cycles.

ml:l2:l2.path.widths.statement: The neighbourhood's request datapath is 256 bits wide (a 512-bit write takes two cycles and is re-joined before the bank FIFO); its response datapath and the ET-Link into each bank are 512 bits; the minion's own fill interface is 256 bits, so a 64 B line reaches the L1 in two beats.
ml:l2:l2.path.widths.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.14-15 §4.3, p.19 §4.3.5, p.20 §4.4, p.22-23 §4.4.3; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.10 §1.1

ml:l2:l2.perfmon.statement: Each bank has a performance monitor: a cycle counter and two 40-bit event counters, which can count RBUF hits, tag hits and misses, victims and opcodes. They are M-mode registers. A U-mode kernel can only read them (syscall 9) with the firmware's default qualifier, which counts all read-type requests and does not separate hits from misses.

ml:l2:l2.rail.hv-logic.statement: Whether VDD_SRAM also powers the rest of the HV region (request queues, crossbars, read buffers, ECC, the voltage-crossing FIFO cells, the instruction-cache memories) or only the RAM macros is not stated. The Power Spec that would say is not in the documents we have.
ml:l2:l2.rail.hv-logic.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.18 §5 (refers to the Power Spec)

ml:l2:l2.rail.sram.statement: The card's VDD_SRAM regulator feeds the shire-cache SRAM arrays (L2/L3/scratchpad); it is one of the three rails whose power the PMIC meters. In every measurement here its set point was 705 mV (703-707 mV read on the die); 750 mV is the card's power-tree figure (20 A / 15 W) and the firmware's boot default.
ml:l2:l2.rail.sram.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl and horace2-telemetry.jsonl (reg_mv.sram = 705 in all 586 + 1,247 samples, die_mv.sram 704); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:46 (power tree), :189-190 (boot defaults: 'SRAM 750'; thermal_pwr_mgmt.h; bl2_pmic_controller.h:165-244)

ml:l2:l2.ramdelay.statement: RAM access time is 2, 3 or 4 cycles, one setting (esr_sc_ram_delay) for all three RAM types, set at boot. The design intends 2, which is the default.
ml:l2:l2.ramdelay.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.9, pdf p.48 §2.14.6.1, pdf p.101; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:260
ml:l2:l2.ramdelay.note: The value programmed on the cards has not been read.

ml:l2:l2.rbuf.statement: Read buffer (RBUF): an 8-entry fully associative mini-cache of clean lines per bank (2 KB per shire). Lines are installed on L2 and scratchpad read hits. Requests are checked against it when they are allocated a reqq entry, and hits are served from it without touching the RAM panels, 'as these memory panels are slow and power hungry'. Anything that will change the data RAM clears the entry, and a 4-entry FIFO holds hit responses.

ml:l2:l2.rbuf.enabled.statement: The RBUF is on by default (esr_sc_l2_rbuf_enable = esr_sc_scp_rbuf_enable = 1 in the RTL's ESR init), and the cards show it: a 36-cycle plateau for working sets of 768 B to 2 KB, then 47 cycles from 4 KB, on all three cards.

ml:l2:l2.rbuf.storage.statement: What the RBUF is built from on silicon is not documented. The Ainekko reimplementation keeps it as 8 x 512-bit registers (flip-flops) holding ECC-corrected data, with an LRU replacement arbiter and a 7-stage pending-install pipeline.

ml:l2:l2.reqq.statement: Each bank has a 64-entry request queue (reqq), the equivalent of MSHRs. An entry lives from allocation through miss, mesh read, fill and any victim write-back. Two entries can be allocated per cycle (one neighbourhood, one L3-slave request), and 21 of the 64 are reserved for L3-slave requests by default.

ml:l2:l2.reqq.arb.statement: Choosing what enters the pipeline takes three steps: round-robin per sub-bank (neighbourhood and L3 separately), then L3 requests before neighbourhood requests, then masking out busy sub-banks and a round-robin across sub-banks. Errata RTLMIN-6207 and 6214 record that a neighbourhood request can starve behind L3-slave traffic.
ml:l2:l2.reqq.arb.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.36 §2.6 Figure 8; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf, pdf p.80-81 §4.1-4.2
ml:l2:l2.reqq.arb.page: One hot line stops a shire

ml:l2:l2.sc.what.statement: Each minion shire has one 4 MB shire cache whose storage is split by ESRs into three partitions: L2 (private to the shire), a slice of the chip-wide L3, and scratchpad. The L2 part serves the shire's 4 neighbourhoods (32 minions) and its RBOX.
ml:l2:l2.sc.what.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.6 §1 and p.8 §1.1; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13 §2.1.3.1

ml:l2:l2.serial-lookup.statement: The lookup is serial (tag first, then data): the data-RAM address includes the way, and the data stages (dap..dc) start after the tag compare (tc), so a hit reads only the hit way's row, not all four ways.
ml:l2:l2.serial-lookup.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:253 (SC_DATA_RAM_ADDR_SIZE = way + set); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.44 read-hit stage figure

ml:l2:l2.sets.statement: A sub-bank holds 4,096 lines = 1,024 sets x 4 ways (4 MB / 64 B / 4 banks / 4 sub-banks).

ml:l2:l2.stages.statement: Read-hit pipeline stages (2-cycle RAMs): ag (reqq allocate), ad (dependencies), rqa (reqq arbitration), tap, ta, ta0, ta1 (tag and tag-state RAM access), te (tag ECC), tc (tag compare: hit, victim), dap, da, da0, da1 (data RAM access), de (data ECC), dc (data complete: OR'd across the sub-banks, then to the response mux, or the dataq if the mux is busy).

ml:l2:l2.stages.budget.statement: If each named stage is one cycle, the 15 stages from reqq allocation to data complete account for 15 of the spec's 21-cycle L2 hit, leaving about 6 cycles for the request crossbar, response mux and response crossbar. The spec cites an 'L2 and L3 Pipeline stages Spreadsheet' that has the real budget, which we do not have.
ml:l2:l2.stages.budget.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.11 Table 1, pdf p.44-46, pdf p.131 ref. 3
ml:l2:l2.stages.budget.note: One cycle per stage is an assumption.

ml:l2:l2.storage-question.statement: What the storage circuit is on silicon is not settled. The Shire Cache Specification calls the data array 'SRAM memory panels' and the datasheet calls it 140 MB of SRAM, but the lab lead said the chip is 'not using SRAM'. No source gives the bitcell (6T, 8T or other) or confirms that the v1.1 macros are the ones taped out.
ml:l2:l2.storage-question.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.40 §2.8 and p.48 §2.14.5; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 §1
ml:l2:l2.storage-question.note: For contrast, the L1 data cache is documented as not SRAM: 4 LRAM (latch-RAM) blocks of 128 rows x 64 bits (external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf, pdf p.29). The remark may refer to the L1 and register files rather than the shire cache.

ml:l2:l2.subbank-busy.statement: With 2-cycle RAMs a sub-bank accepts a new request only every other cycle (3-cycle RAMs: every third). Operations that need two RAM passes (a fill that may evict, an atomic) reserve bubble slots, because the pipeline never stalls once a request is scheduled.

ml:l2:l2.subbanks.statement: Each bank is four sub-banks. Each sub-bank has its own tag RAM, tag-state RAM, data RAM and ECC logic; the read buffer, atomic unit and coalescing buffer are shared by the bank's four sub-banks.
ml:l2:l2.subbanks.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.35 §2.5; pdf p.9 ('4 sub-banks/bank' is the POR for the first SoC)

ml:l2:l2.tag-ram.statement: Tag RAM: one row per set holding all four ways' tags, each 23 bits + 6 ECC bits, so the row is 116 bits and the four tags are read and compared in parallel.
ml:l2:l2.tag-ram.note: The overview (pdf p.9) says '7 bits of ECC stored with each 33-bit tag'; §2.14.2, the defines and the 1024x116 macro all say 23 + 6.

ml:l2:l2.tag-state-ram.statement: Tag-state RAM: one 40-bit row per set = 4 x {valid, locked, zero, qwen[3:0]} + 5-bit LRU code + 7-bit ECC. It is read and written on every L2 request, and it is two-ported, so the read and the LRU/dirty update happen in the same pass.
ml:l2:l2.tag-state-ram.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf (v1.1), pdf p.47 §2.14.3 Table 12 and pdf p.45; external/core-et/rtl/inc/shire_cache_defines.vh:231-237

ml:l2:l2.throughput.statement: Consecutive operations to different sub-banks can issue every cycle. Operations that can create a victim (fills, writes, write-arounds, locks) run at one per 4, 6 or 8 cycles per sub-bank (RAM delay 2, 3, 4), because read and write slots are both reserved. The tag is written 4 cycles after the victim is chosen (2-cycle RAMs).

ml:l2:l2.transistors.statement: If the single-port data and tag macros use a 6-transistor cell and the two-port tag-state file an 8-transistor cell (the usual choice for such macros), one shire's cache arrays hold about 243 million cell transistors (39.6 Mbit x 6 + 0.66 Mbit x 8), before any periphery.
ml:l2:l2.transistors.note: GENERIC assumption: the ET bitcell is not documented (see l2.storage-question).

ml:l2:l2.trim.statement: Each logical RAM group has ESR trim bits: RM (read margin), RME (RM enable), RA (read assist), WA (write assist) and WPULSE (write-pulse width). They default to 'RM0 mode to allow nominal 650mV operation'. For the 1PUHD tag and data macros the table gives RM0 = VMIN 585 mV, Vnom 650: RM 0, WA 7, RA 1, WPULSE 0. For the 2PUHDRF tag-state RAM it gives RM0 = VMIN 540 mV: WA 6, RA 2. The tables run up to RM5 at 855 mV VMIN.

ml:l2:l2.trim.reset.statement: The simulator's reset values for shire_cache_ram_cfg1/2 (0xE800340, 0x03A0), decoded with the HAL's field layout, are exactly the tables' RM0 rows: tag and data RAMs RM=0, RA=1, WA=7, WPULSE=0 with RME=0; tag-state RA=2, WA=6. No firmware in et-platform at 836a4ab writes these registers.
ml:l2:l2.trim.reset.source: external/et-platform/sw-sysemu/esrs_et.cpp:46-47; external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/etsoc_shire_other_esr.h:3070-3376 (field bit positions); grep of et-platform for RAM_CFG writes (none)
ml:l2:l2.trim.reset.note: Whether the boot ROM or silicon reset programs something else is not known (ask). If they do not, the arrays run with the 650 mV assist settings at the rail's ~705 mV.

ml:l2:l2.vc-fifo.statement: The neighbourhood's per-bank output FIFOs double as the clock- and voltage-crossing elements: semi-synchronous VC FIFOs from the cell library, with level shifters built in at the HV/LV boundary. Their storage cells always sit in the HV region 'as performance and access time improve with the voltage'. Responses cross back through a VC FIFO at the neighbourhood's input.
ml:l2:l2.vc-fifo.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.18-19 §4.3.4, pdf p.20 §4.4.1, pdf p.45 §7.1 (Figure 16)

ml:l2:l2.voltage.idle.statement: Measured on-die SRAM-rail voltage per shire at idle: 703-707 mV across the 34 minion shires (minion rail 513-522 mV, mesh 483-486 mV).

ml:l2:l2.voltage.limits.statement: The firmware limits the SRAM rail to 660-850 mV, and DVFS moves the minion and L2/SRAM voltages together.

ml:l2:l2.xbar.req.statement: req_xbar: a full crossbar from the 5 clients (4 neighbourhoods + RBOX) to the 4 banks + UC. Each bank has one catch FIFO per neighbourhood and a round-robin arbiter that skips entries whose bank is stalled. It lives in the shire-cache hierarchy 'so that it can be routed on top of all four banks'.

ml:l2:l2.xbar.rsp.statement: rsp_xbar: the same module in reverse (4 banks + UC to 4 neighbourhoods + RBOX). Neighbourhoods never back-pressure, since space for the response is reserved. It arbitrates only when two banks answer the same neighbourhood in one cycle.

ml:l3:g.6t-cell.statement: GENERIC. A 6T SRAM cell stores a bit on two cross-coupled inverters (two PMOS pull-ups, two NMOS pull-downs) and connects to a bitline pair through two NMOS access transistors whose gates are the row's wordline.
ml:l3:g.6t-cell.source: textbook (e.g. Rabaey, Digital Integrated Circuits, ch. 12)
ml:l3:g.6t-cell.note: The ET-SoC-1 sources name the data array 'SRAM' but not its bitcell: u.bitcell.

ml:l3:g.assist.statement: GENERIC. Read assist usually lowers the wordline voltage so a read cannot flip a weak cell; read-margin settings delay the sense-amplifier enable so more bitline swing develops, slower but safer at low voltage.
ml:l3:g.assist.note: The ET macros expose RA and RM (l3.trim-table); their exact circuit effect is vendor-specific.

ml:l3:g.crossing.statement: GENERIC. A voltage and clock crossing: a level shifter (cross-coupled PMOS over an NMOS differential input pair) lifts or drops the signal swing, and a 2-flip-flop synchroniser (as the spec's VCFIFO uses) samples it in the receiving clock, costing 2-3 receiving-clock cycles.
ml:l3:g.crossing.source: textbook; the 2 stages are et-spec (external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.11)

ml:l3:g.ecc.statement: GENERIC. SECDED (72,64) Hamming code: 8 check bits per 64 data bits computed by XOR trees on write; on read a syndrome from the same XOR trees points at a single flipped bit, which an XOR corrects, and flags a double error.
ml:l3:g.ecc.note: That the shire cache uses 8 ECC bits per 64-bit doubleword is et-spec (l3.geometry).

ml:l3:g.icg.statement: GENERIC. An integrated clock gate is a latch (transparent while the clock is low) holding the enable, ANDed with the clock: when the enable is low the macro's clock does not toggle, so its clock tree and flops draw no switching power.

ml:l3:g.leakage.statement: GENERIC. Every SRAM cell leaks all the time: sub-threshold current flows through its off transistors (one pull-up or pull-down per inverter and the access transistors), rising roughly exponentially with temperature.
ml:l3:g.leakage.note: Matches the measured SRAM rail at idle (l3.leakage).

ml:l3:g.panel-read-count.statement: GENERIC, if each panel is an ordinary compiled SRAM macro: a line read raises one wordline in each of the 4 panels and fires 576 sense amplifiers (144 per panel); how many bitline pairs swing depends on the column mux, which the macro datasheets would settle.
ml:l3:g.panel-read-count.source: textbook (GENERIC); widths from l2.seq.load-hit.09; the column mux is l2.macro.name-decode (unknown)

ml:l3:g.read.statement: GENERIC. A read: precharge/equalise PMOS hold both bitlines at the supply and switch off; the row decoder's NAND/NOR gates select one wordline driver, which raises that wordline across the row; in every cell of the row the access transistor on the side storing 0 pulls its bitline down through the pull-down NMOS, developing tens of mV; the column mux passes one pair per output bit to a latch-type sense amplifier, which fires on its enable and resolves to full rail into the output latch.
ml:l3:g.read.note: Every column of the selected row discharges one bitline whatever the data, so the array's read energy is roughly data-independent; data-dependent energy comes from the output datapath, ECC and wires.

ml:l3:g.router.statement: GENERIC. A mesh router stage: input virtual-channel buffers (flip-flop or register-file arrays), route computation, virtual-channel and switch allocators (arbiters), a crossbar of multiplexers, and output drivers onto the link; each link is a bundle of wires broken by repeaters (inverter pairs) every few hundred microns.
ml:l3:g.router.source: textbook (Dally and Towles, Principles and Practices of Interconnection Networks)
ml:l3:g.router.note: ET routers have 8 ports and 4 VC slots each, 9 main layers per stop (chip fact L105; SYNTHESIS.md:67-68).

ml:l3:g.tag-compare.statement: GENERIC. Tag compare: per way, 23 XNOR gates (one per tag bit) feed an AND tree (or a precharged match line pulled down by any mismatch); the four hit signals select the way and encode it.

ml:l3:g.wire-energy.statement: GENERIC. A wire's switching energy is about C x V^2 per 0-to-1 transition (C about 0.2 pF/mm), so random data (a transition on about half the bits) costs several times zeros; repeaters add to it.

ml:l3:g.write.statement: GENERIC. A write: write drivers pull one bitline of each selected pair to ground, the wordline rises, and the access transistor overpowers the cell's PMOS pull-up so the cell flips. Write assist (for example a negative bitline or a lowered cell supply) and a longer write pulse make the flip reliable at low voltage.
ml:l3:g.write.note: The ET macros expose WA and WPULSE trims (l3.trim-table); which technique WA drives is not stated.

ml:l3:l3.clock.statement: The shire cache runs on shire_clock, the same clock as the minions (the neighbourhood clock is shire_clock shifted 180 degrees; the errata: every area of a minion shire except the NoC uses the same clock), so 600 MHz on these cards; the mesh runs on clk__noc, 400 MHz.
ml:l3:l3.clock.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf pdf p.12 Table 2; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf pdf p.42; clk__noc 400 MHz: telemetry mhz.noc (docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl) and SYNTHESIS.md:72

ml:l3:l3.clock-gating.statement: Each data macro's clock is gated: an integrated clock gate (latch + AND) opens only while the pipeline accesses that sub-bank and for ram_delay cycles after; the spec asks that address and write-enable inputs stay unchanged when a RAM is not accessed.
ml:l3:l3.clock-gating.source: external/core-et-main/hw/ip/shirecache/rtl/shirecache_pipe_data_ram_wrap.sv:52-72; external/core-et-main/AGENTS.md:100 (prim_clk_gate: 'latch + AND (ASIC ICG pattern)'); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.46 §2.14.1.5, §2.14.1.11

ml:l3:l3.dram-leg.statement: Past the L3 a DRAM load adds 91 + 12 cycles per hop from the home to the memory shire (the constant 90-91 on three cards).

ml:l3:l3.energy-per-load.statement: Per 64 B line read from the L3 by 1 KB tensor loads through the mesh (a working set whose lines are homed across the chip), on random data: 1,233, 1,203 and 1,461 pJ above idle (19.3, 18.8 and 22.8 pJ/B), of which 39, 39 and 28% on the SRAM rail (the L2 miss, the L3 read and the L2 fill), 39% on the mesh rail, 7, 6 and 7% on the minion rail and 14, 16 and 27% on no metered rail (aifoundry2, aifoundry3 and aifoundry1 card 1). Each mesh hop adds 115 pJ per line on random data and 43 on zeros (1.80 and 0.67 pJ/B, the mean of the energy manual's straight lines through another shire's scratchpad at 1-8 hops).
ml:l3:l3.energy-per-load.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.cards.<card>.summary['dramrow/stride8K/random'] (rails_over_w, over_idle_w, pj_per_byte) and catalogue.cards.<card>.wire.<zeros|random>.slope_pj_per_byte_per_hop, as Anatomy of a memory access §6 gives them (workloads/memprobe/build_report.py)
